issues.title: marketplace: harden pack output for downstream marketplaces (pluginRoot subtraction + remote pass-through fields)
issues.body:
## Context

[github/awesome-copilot#1570](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/pull/1570) adopts `apm pack` for its marketplace generation (73 plugins from one `apm.yml`). Code review on that PR ([review #4202980531](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/pull/1570#pullrequestreview-4202980531)) surfaced two independent shortcomings in APM's marketplace builder that together prevent the PR from being a clean drop-in replacement for the bespoke generator:

1. **Local-source `pluginRoot` double-prefix** -- breaks runtime resolution.
2. **Remote-source pass-through metadata dropped** -- forces a bridge script to retain `plugins/external.json`.

Filing both as one umbrella because they share the theme "make `apm pack`'s marketplace.json output spec-equivalent to what hand-rolled generators produce today" and both are small, additive builder changes.

---

## Finding 1 -- Local sources double-prefix `metadata.pluginRoot`

### Symptom

awesome-copilot's existing baseline (`staged` branch) emits:

```json
{ "name": "ai-team-orchestration", "source": "ai-team-orchestration", ... }
```

with `metadata.pluginRoot: "./plugins"`. A spec-compliant consumer joins the two as `./plugins/ai-team-orchestration`.

`apm pack` today emits:

```json
{ "name": "ai-team-orchestration", "source": "./plugins/ai-team-orchestration", ... }
```

against the same `pluginRoot`. The consumer joins to `./plugins/./plugins/ai-team-orchestration` -- a path that does not exist. This is a behavior break, not a cosmetic delta.

### Root cause

`LOCAL_SOURCE_RE = re.compile(r"^\./")` ([`yml_schema.py:72`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/marketplace/yml_schema.py#L72)) requires the leading `./` for an apm.yml `source` value to be classified as local -- so authors **must** write `source: ./plugins/foo` in apm.yml.

The builder then emits that source verbatim ([`builder.py:730`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/marketplace/builder.py#L730)):

```python
if is_local:
    plugin["source"] = entry.source  # never subtracts metadata.pluginRoot
```

`MarketplaceConfig.plugin_root` is parsed and re-emitted into `metadata.pluginRoot` ([`models.py:85,199`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/marketplace/models.py#L85)), but never consulted on the emit path. The result is structurally inconsistent output: APM declares `pluginRoot` but doesn't honor it in its own sources.

### Proposed fix

In the local-source emit branch of `builder.py`, when `metadata.pluginRoot` is set:

```python
if is_local:
    source_value = entry.source
    if config.plugin_root:
        source_value = _strip_plugin_root(source_value, config.plugin_root)
    plugin["source"] = source_value
```

Where `_strip_plugin_root("./plugins/foo", "./plugins")` returns `"foo"`. Idempotent (no leading `./` -> no strip), pure path arithmetic, no I/O.

### Why now

Workaround in awesome-copilot is a 5-line post-process in `eng/merge-external-plugins.mjs`. Acceptable as a stopgap but it couples a downstream repo's bridge to APM's emit format. Native fix removes that coupling permanently.

### Acceptance

- [ ] When `metadata.pluginRoot` is set, local sources in `marketplace.json` are emitted with the prefix stripped.
- [ ] `metadata.pluginRoot` continues to round-trip unchanged.
- [ ] No-op when `pluginRoot` is unset (today's behavior preserved).
- [ ] Unit tests: (a) prefix stripped when `pluginRoot` matches, (b) pass-through when no match, (c) no `pluginRoot` -> verbatim emission.

---

## Finding 2 -- Remote `PackageEntry` drops author/keywords/license/repository

### Symptom

awesome-copilot's `plugins/external.json` entries publish four fields that vanish through `apm pack`:

```json
{
  "name": "azure",
  "author": { "name": "Microsoft", "url": "https://www.microsoft.com" },
  "keywords": ["azure", "cloud", ...],
  "license": "MIT",
  "repository": "https://github.com/microsoft/github-copilot-for-azure",
  "source": { ... }
}
```

`apm pack` today emits only `description`/`version`/`tags` as pass-through; the four fields above are silently dropped.

### Root cause

`_PACKAGE_ENTRY_KEYS` in [`yml_schema.py:88-99`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/marketplace/yml_schema.py#L88) does not list them. Even if a maintainer writes them in `apm.yml`, the parser rejects unknown keys.

A second smaller issue stacked on the same surface: for remote entries, `description`/`version` come from the remote repo's own `apm.yml` only. Third-party plugin repos (`microsoft/Dataverse-skills`, `dotnet/skills`, `figma/mcp-server-guide`) don't ship one, so those fields render empty even when the maintainer supplied values in awesome-copilot's `apm.yml`.

### Proposed fix

**Schema (additive):** extend `_PACKAGE_ENTRY_KEYS` to permit `author`, `keywords`, `license`, `repository`. Validate types (object / array / string / string).

**Builder:** for remote entries:
- emit the four new fields verbatim when present;
- when `entry.description` / `entry.version` are set in apm.yml, prefer them over the remote-fetched values (today the remote fetch wins).

### Out of scope here

The source-object key delta (`{type, repository, ref, commit}` vs legacy `{source, repo, path}`) is a downstream consumer concern. APM should keep emitting its own canonical shape; consumers adapt at publish time. Filing as a separate decision if it ever becomes a real blocker.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `marketplace.packages[]` accepts `author`, `keywords`, `license`, `repository`.
- [ ] Remote-source builder emits those fields verbatim when present on the entry.
- [ ] When `entry.description` / `entry.version` are set on a remote entry, they override the remote fetch.
- [ ] Unit tests: (a) all four pass-through fields round-trip, (b) maintainer description overrides remote, (c) absent fields produce identical output to today.

---

## Why ship both together

Both are small, additive, zero-risk-when-unset builder changes on the same code path. Together they let `awesome-copilot` collapse:
- `eng/merge-external-plugins.mjs` (drops with Finding 2 closure)
- the post-process step that strips `pluginRoot` (drops with Finding 1 closure)
- `plugins/external.json` (drops with Finding 2 closure -- moves into `apm.yml`)

End state: `apm pack` becomes a true drop-in replacement for the bespoke generator -- which is the proof point this work was designed to deliver.

## Tracking

- Downstream PR consuming both: [github/awesome-copilot#1570](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/pull/1570)
- Downstream issue: [github/awesome-copilot#1569](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/issues/1569)

issues.title: Strangler-fig: progressively tighten Ruff complexity thresholds
issues.body:
# Strangler-fig: progressively tighten Ruff complexity thresholds

**Labels:** `tracking`, `code-quality`

---

## Overview

PR #999 introduced Ruff code quality guardrails with complexity thresholds set just above current codebase maximums (strangler-fig pattern). This tracking issue coordinates the progressive tightening of those thresholds through dedicated refactoring PRs.

## Current thresholds (baseline from #999)

| Metric | Threshold | Current max | Worst offender |
|--------|-----------|-------------|----------------|
| max-statements | 275 | 269 | `mcp_integrator.py::install` |
| max-branches | 115 | 108 | `mcp_integrator.py::install` |
| max-complexity | 100 | 97 | `mcp_integrator.py::install` |
| max-args | 18 | 18 | `commands/install.py` |
| max-returns | 18 | 16 | `marketplace/publisher.py` |
| file-length (CI) | 2400 | 2316 | `github_downloader.py` |

## Strangler-fig roadmap

| Metric | Current | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3 | Target |
|--------|---------|---------|---------|---------|--------|
| max-statements | 275 | 200 | 120 | 80 | 50 |
| max-branches | 115 | 60 | 40 | 25 | 15 |
| max-complexity | 100 | 50 | 35 | 20 | 10 |
| max-args | 18 | 15 | 12 | 8 | 5 |
| max-returns | 18 | 12 | 8 | 6 | 6 |
| file-length | 2400 | 1400 | 800 | 500 | 400 |

## Approach

Each stage is a separate sub-issue. A stage PR must:

1. Refactor the functions that exceed the new threshold
2. Update the thresholds in `pyproject.toml`
3. Pass `uv run ruff check src/ tests/` with the tightened values
4. Not change functional behaviour (refactor only)

## Sub-issues

- [ ] Stage 1: Tame the worst outliers (~5 files)
- [ ] Stage 2: Second-tier tightening (~15 files)
- [ ] Stage 3: Broad refactoring pass (~35 files)
- [ ] Stage 4: Reach target thresholds (~80 files)

## References

- PR #999: Ruff guardrails (merged)
- #1003: Audit F401 noqa suppressions
- #1004: Stage 1 draft (superseded by this roadmap)
- #1005: Enable RUF002/RUF003

issues.title: Refactor apm-review-panel: VERDICT regime -> ADVISORY regime (drop binary APPROVE/REJECT, add doc-writer, restructure comment)
issues.body:
## Problem

The current **APM Review Panel** skill (`apm-review-panel`) is structurally adversarial: it computes a binary `APPROVE` / `REJECT` verdict and writes a `panel-approved` / `panel-rejected` label. The schema forces every finding into one of two buckets — `required[]` (blocks merge, deterministically forces `REJECT`) or `nits[]` (skip-if-you-want). There is no middle ground.

In practice this produces two failure modes:

1. **Over-strict verdicts.** A panelist reading carefully will lean `required` for any real-but-not-blocking issue, because `nit` reads as "ignore me" and the schema offers no third slot. One careful panelist with one borderline `required` finding flips the entire panel to `REJECT`.
2. **Adversarial comment shape.** The comment top-loads `Verdict: REJECT` + `Required before merge (N items)` — a gating frame, not a collaborative one. PR authors (especially external contributors) read it as "the bots want me to fix N things" instead of "here is the panel's recommendation, the maintainer decides".

### Concrete reference: PR #1084 (manual local panel run)

When PR #1084 (a 101+/1- bug-fix from external contributor `@tillig` unblocking GHES/GitLab/Bitbucket users) was reviewed manually using the same persona threads but a different output template, the comment ([link](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/pull/1084#issuecomment-4358506208)):

- top-loaded **CEO arbitration prose** (why this matters strategically)
- followed with a **principle alignment** block (multi-host, pragmatic-as-npm)
- carried a **per-persona summary table** (one line per persona, verdict + nit-count + one-liner)
- rendered **two mermaid diagrams** (component flow + sequence) directly in the body, not buried in `extras`
- listed **3 prioritized post-merge follow-ups** (none blocking)
- ended with **ship recommendation prose** ("merge as-is")
- collapsed full per-persona findings at the bottom

This is the shape the current panel should produce. It actually helps the contributor and the human reviewer; it does not pretend to be a gate.

## Proposal

Refactor `apm-review-panel` from a **VERDICT regime** to an **ADVISORY regime** (mapping onto genesis example 04, not example 05).

### What changes

| Aspect | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| **Verdict** | `APPROVE` / `REJECT`, deterministic | None. Comment carries CEO ship-recommendation prose; maintainer + author decide. |
| **Severity model** | `required[]` (gates) + `nits[]` (skip) | `findings[]` with `severity: blocking \| recommended \| nit`. `blocking` reserved for real correctness/security regressions with explicit rationale. |
| **Labels written** | `panel-approved` XOR `panel-rejected`, plus `panel-review` removal | Only `panel-review` removal (trigger idempotency). No verdict labels. |
| **Comment top** | `Verdict: REJECT` + `Required before merge (N)` | CEO framing paragraph + principle alignment + per-persona summary table |
| **Mermaid diagrams** | Buried in `python-architect.extras.diagrams`; often missing | Template-required: component diagram + sequence diagram in the body |
| **Roster** | py-arch, cli-log, devx, sec, growth, [auth] | + **doc-writer** (conditional like auth-expert: docs/, README, CHANGELOG, .apm/skills/, .github/agents/, instructions/, .github/workflows/*.md) |
| **Companion workflow** | `pr-panel-label-reset.yml` strips verdict labels on every push | Becomes obsolete (no verdict labels to strip) — delete or downscope |

### Why this is better

- **Helpful to contributors.** The advisory frame matches the mental model of code review on an OSS repo: a panel of reviewers leaving recommendations, not a CI gate. External contributors are not punished by a bot verdict.
- **Helpful to maintainers.** A summary table + mermaid diagrams + ship-recommendation prose lets the human reviewer scan in 10 seconds. Today's verdict comment is longer and less informative.
- **Honest about LLM panels.** Binary deterministic verdicts give false confidence — they hide real disagreement under a `sum(required) == 0` calculation. Advisory framing makes the panel's actual signal (recommendations, not decisions) explicit.
- **Aligned with APM principles.** Pragmatic-as-npm: npm does not have a binary "your package quality is REJECTED" gate; it has scanners and recommendations. The panel should mirror that.
- **Doc-writer fills a real gap.** Documentation drift is a frequent finding raised informally today; making it a first-class persona surfaces it consistently.

### Reference

The good comment from PR #1084: https://github.com/microsoft/apm/pull/1084#issuecomment-4358506208

The PR refactoring this skill will land alongside this issue and explain WHY/WHAT/HOW with the same diagrams and trade-off analysis.

## Out of scope

- Changing the persona definitions themselves (each `.agent.md` continues to load and reason as today; only the orchestration contract and output shape change).
- Changing the trigger surface (`panel-review` label + `workflow_dispatch` continue to work).
- Auto-resolving severity disputes (the CEO arbitration paragraph already handles this; the schema just needs to express the dispute, not gate on it).

issues.title: Claude support - name collisions because plugins are deployed without namespacing
issues.body:
Claude Code natively namespaces plugin commands and skills using a plugin:name convention. Plugin developers rely on this — they use short, generic names like analyze, review, or summarize, expecting the plugin name to disambiguate (e.g., ci:analyze vs jira:analyze).

APM's support for installing Claude Code plugins is a killer feature, but it currently deploys skills and commands using bare names with no namespace prefix. When two plugins define a skill with the same name (e.g., both ci and jira define analyze), the last-installed package silently overwrites the first. A warning is emitted, but there's no way to have both coexist.

This is a real problem in practice because generic skill names are the norm in the plugin ecosystem — developers aren't defensive about naming because Claude Code's native install handles it for them.

Current behavior:

  - Skills deploy to .claude/skills/analyze/ — bare name, no namespace
  - Commands deploy to .claude/commands/analyze.md — same
  - Last-installed wins on collision (with a warning)
  - apm run supports qualified paths as a workaround for prompts, but skills have no equivalent


This would be a big change to apm's behavior, so it would need a careful design, but I wanted to check if you were open to changing this behavior?

  - Skills and commands should be namespaced to match Claude Code's convention (e.g., plugin-analyze)
  - Two plugins defining analyze should coexist without collision
  - The namespacing scheme should be compatible with how Claude Code discovers and invokes plugin skills

issues.title: [FEATURE] Marketplace upstreams: curated pass-through with allow-list governance
issues.body:
## Problem

Today APM's marketplace has two disjoint sides:

- **Authoring** (`apm.yml -> marketplace:`): each `packages[]` entry's `source` must be a single git repo (`owner/repo`) or a local path. There is no way to express "include a plugin from another marketplace".
- **Consumption** (`~/.apm/marketplaces.json`): registers external `marketplace.json` URLs for `browse` / `search` / `update`. Read-only from the curator's perspective.

A curator (e.g. an enterprise running an internal marketplace) wants to selectively re-expose plugins from external marketplaces (e.g. a Claude Code marketplace such as `abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus`), with curator-side allow-list control over which plugins reach their consumers.

## Proposed solution: marketplace upstreams

Add a first-class **upstream** concept to the curator authoring surface:

- New `upstreams:` block in `apm.yml -> marketplace:` registers external marketplace pointers under a curator-chosen alias.
- New `upstream:` field on `packages[]` entries declares an allow-listed entry that resolves to a plugin from a registered upstream.
- The builder fetches the upstream `marketplace.json` (atomic read at a pinned manifest SHA), strict-parses it, looks up the plugin, resolves its source to an immutable commit SHA, and emits a vanilla plugin entry into the curator's `marketplace.json`.

### v1 product contract

**v1 is curated upstream / governance-only**, not artifact custody:

- Curator controls *which* plugins are exposed and *at what version*.
- Curator's lockfile pins manifest SHA + plugin SHA for reproducible curator builds.
- Consumers still fetch plugin content from the upstream git host at install time.
- Never called "mirror" in v1 prose -- "mirror" is reserved for a future v2 `distribution: rehost` mode that would add true artifact custody.

One-line pitch: *"Allow-list governance over external plugins, pinned to immutable commits, with provenance baked into every build -- without running an artifact server."*

### Trust model

| Concern | v1 status |
|---|---|
| Allow-list governance | YES (curator picks which plugins are exposed) |
| Build-time commit pinning | YES (curator's lockfile pins manifest SHA + plugin SHA) |
| Reproducible curator builds | YES (rebuild from lock = byte-identical output) |
| Consumer-side artifact custody | NO -- consumer clones from upstream git host at install |
| Resilience to upstream takedown / force-push | NO -- consumer install fails opaquely if upstream rewrites history |
| Defence against upstream repo rename / takeover | YES (canonical-owner check) |

## Sketch of the surface

```yaml
marketplace:
  upstreams:
    - alias: gitnexus
      repo: abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus
      path: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json   # default
      ref: <sha-or-tag>                        # required for reproducibility
      branch: main                             # used only when ref absent and allow_head=true
      host: github.com                         # default
      allow_head: false                        # default
  packages:
    # Direct package (existing shape)
    - name: my-skill
      source: owner/repo
      version: ">=1.0.0"

    # Upstream-sourced package (new shape)
    - name: my-renamed-skill                  # display name in curator's marketplace
      upstream: gitnexus                      # references upstreams[].alias
      plugin: original-name                   # name in upstream marketplace; defaults to `name`
      version: ">=2.0.0"                      # optional curator override
      ref: <sha-or-tag>                       # optional curator override
      description: "ACME-curated ..."         # optional override
      tags: [acme, approved]                  # optional override
      allow_head: false                       # opt-in to mutable refs (per-entry)
```

```bash
apm marketplace upstream add <owner/repo> [--alias --path --ref --branch --host --allow-head]
apm marketplace upstream list [--verbose]
apm marketplace upstream remove <alias> [--yes]
apm marketplace upstream refresh [<alias>]   # shows diff before advancing lock pins
apm marketplace upstream browse <alias>      # lists plugins available in upstream
apm marketplace package add --upstream <alias> <plugin-name> [--name --version --ref --tags]
```

## Key design decisions (panel-reviewed)

The plan was reviewed by an APM panel (supply-chain, architect, devx, primitives, test-coverage, CEO). Findings folded in:

- **Provenance lives in `apm.lock.yaml` only.** No `metadata.apm.*` keys in `marketplace.json` -- preserves the Anthropic-conformance hard rule at `src/apm_cli/marketplace/builder.py:13-15`.
- **Type-level discriminated union:** `DirectPackageEntry` / `UpstreamPackageEntry` as separate frozen dataclasses (not optional fields on a single class).
- **Module decomposition:** new `marketplace/upstream_parser.py` (strict parser, separate from lenient consumer parser), `marketplace/upstream_resolver.py` (extracted resolver -- avoids `MarketplaceBuilder` god-class), `marketplace/upstream_cache.py` (separate from consumer `client.py`).
- **Cache key uses `__` (double-underscore)**, not `::` -- colons are illegal in Windows filenames (CI runs on `windows-latest`).
- **Per-upstream-host auth**: `AuthResolver.resolve(upstream_host, org=upstream_owner)` with `unauth_first=True` for public repos, never inheriting curator's marketplace-source PAT.
- **Repo-rename / takeover guard**: every fetch verifies GitHub Contents API `repository.full_name` matches configured `upstreams[alias].repo`; lockfile records canonical name.
- **Cross-shape `name` uniqueness** enforced builder-side (prevents dependency-confusion / name shadowing).
- **Round-trip invariant**: every emitted plugin must survive `parse_marketplace_json` (catches lenient-vs-strict parser drift).
- **Atomic single-fetch invariant**: manifest is fetched once at the pinned SHA; no re-fetch during resolution.
- **Governance gate**: new policy key `marketplace.upstream.allow_unpinned_refs` lets enterprises forbid `allow_head: true`.
- **`security.md` update required in same PR**: the existing "no intermediary registry, proxy, or mirror" claim becomes inaccurate.
- **`apm doctor` integration**: upstream reachability + pinned-vs-HEAD drift + manifest-SHA round-trip checks.
- **Consumer-side passthrough notice**: when `apm install` resolves a plugin with upstream provenance in the lockfile, output names the upstream so the trust boundary is visible.
- **DevX**: `upstream_name` renamed to `plugin`; CLI mutex enforcement (`source` xor `--upstream`); dual-shape help text; copy-pasteable next-step hints; exit code 2 for resolution errors; `_authoring_commands` registration.
- **Cut from v1**: `apm marketplace upstream search` (browse covers it).
- **Terminology**: "upstream" in user-facing copy; never "mirror" in v1 (reserved for v2 rehost).

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Re-hosting / artifact custody / true air-gap (`distribution: rehost`) -- v2.
- Transitive upstreams (curator upstreams marketplace B which upstreams marketplace C).
- Install-time auto-sync of upstream changes.
- Cross-git-host upstreams (upstream and plugins on different host families).
- Mirroring non-APM/non-Claude formats (npm, PyPI, etc.).

## Implementation plan (high-level, dependency-ordered)

1. Schema: type-level union dataclasses + `upstreams:` block + strict validation.
2. `upstream_parser.py`: strict parser with named rejection reasons.
3. `upstream_cache.py`: Windows-safe content-addressed cache with per-host auth.
4. `upstream_resolver.py`: extracted resolver (atomic fetch, precedence ladder, repo-rename guard).
5. `MarketplaceBuilder` integration: dispatch on union, name-shadowing check, round-trip invariant, exit code 2.
6. `apm.lock.yaml` upstream section: writer + reader; `refresh` diff.
7. CLI surface: `upstream add/list/remove/refresh/browse` + `package add --upstream`.
8. `apm doctor` upstream health checks.
9. Governance policy key `marketplace.upstream.allow_unpinned_refs`.
10. Consumer-side passthrough notice in `apm install` output.
11. Integration tests in `scripts/test-integration.sh` (incl. lock-holds, reproducibility).
12. Docs: new upstreams guide, `security.md` rewrite, policy-reference update, apm-guide skill resources, CHANGELOG.
13. Final lint + format gate.

## Alternatives considered

- **Mirror / proxy**: rejected as v1 framing because no artifacts are re-hosted; reserve "mirror" for the future `distribution: rehost` mode.
- **Optional `source` on `PackageEntry`**: rejected -- breaks unguarded `entry.source` access across the builder; type-level discriminated union is the correct pattern.
- **Provenance keys in `marketplace.json`**: rejected -- violates the Anthropic-conformant emission contract documented in `builder.py:13-15`. All provenance lives in the lockfile.
- **Extending consumer `client.py` for upstream cache**: rejected -- consumer cache is wired to `MarketplaceSource` + consumer auth context. Sibling `upstream_cache.py` keeps boundaries clean.

## Additional context

Plan validated with APM Panel

issues.title: [BUG] Copilot CLI adapter resolves environment variables at install time instead of preserving references
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When `apm install` generates `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` for the `copilot` target, environment variable references (e.g. `${env:COPILOT_MCP_JIRA_PERSONAL_TOKEN}`) are resolved to their actual values at install time and baked into the file as plaintext secrets. 

The Copilot CLI adapter should instead emit `${VARIABLE}` references (stripping the `env:` prefix), because Copilot CLI natively supports runtime variable substitution using `$VAR`, `${VAR}`, and `${VAR:-default}` syntax — as documented in the [official GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/cloud-agent/extend-cloud-agent-with-mcp#variable-substitution).

This issue was introduced by PR #947 (fix for #944), which was based on the incorrect premise that "Copilot CLI `mcp-config.json` has no native interpolation."

**To Reproduce**

1. Define an MCP server in `apm.yml` with environment variable references:
   ```yaml
   target: copilot
   dependencies:
     mcp:
       - name: my-atlassian
         transport: http
         url: https://my-instance.atlassian.net/mcp
         headers:
           "X-Atlassian-Jira-Personal-Token": "${env:COPILOT_MCP_JIRA_PERSONAL_TOKEN}"
   ```
2. Ensure the environment variable `COPILOT_MCP_JIRA_PERSONAL_TOKEN` is set in your shell.
3. Run `apm install`
4. Inspect `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`

**Expected behavior**

The generated `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` should preserve environment variable references using Copilot CLI's native syntax:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-atlassian": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://my-instance.atlassian.net/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-Atlassian-Jira-Personal-Token": "${COPILOT_MCP_JIRA_PERSONAL_TOKEN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Translation rules should be:
| `apm.yml` syntax | `mcp-config.json` output |
|---|---|
| `${env:VAR}` | `${VAR}` |
| `${VAR}` | `${VAR}` |
| `$VAR` | `$VAR` |

This mirrors what the VS Code adapter does (preserving `${env:VAR}` for VS Code's runtime) but adapted to Copilot CLI's documented syntax.

**Actual behavior**

The generated `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` contains the resolved secret values in plaintext:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-atlassian": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://my-instance.atlassian.net/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-Atlassian-Jira-Personal-Token": "<actual-secret-value-resolved-from-env>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Security concern**: This means secrets are stored in plaintext on disk in a user-global config file, which is both a security risk and breaks portability across machines/users.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 11
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.12.2
 - VSCode Version: 1.118.1

**Logs**

N/A — no error is raised; the behavior is silent and incorrect.

**Additional context**

- Original issue: #944 ("[BUG] apm install writes bare `${VAR}` in VS Code `mcp.json` headers")
- Fix PR: #947
- The fix correctly handles the VS Code adapter (translating `${VAR}` → `${env:VAR}`) but incorrectly handles the Copilot CLI adapter by resolving values at install time.
- **GitHub Docs confirming Copilot CLI supports variable substitution**: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/cloud-agent/extend-cloud-agent-with-mcp#variable-substitution

  > The following syntax patterns are supported for referencing environment variables:
  > - `$VAR`
  > - `${VAR}`
  > - `${VAR:-default}`

- The original issue reporter (@kkadete) also noted: "The target 'copilot' should also take this into consideration, but removing the 'env:' in case it exists" — which aligns with the expected behavior described above.

issues.title: Audit unmarked integration tests + swap test-integration.sh to pytest discovery (PR2 of #1166)
issues.body:
Follow-up to #1167 (PR1 of #1166). PR1 landed marker infrastructure in `tests/integration/conftest.py`. This issue tracks the remaining execution-side work: replacing `scripts/test-integration.sh`'s 386-line `run_e2e_tests()` (26 explicit per-file pytest invocations) with a single `pytest tests/integration/` discovery call.

## Why this is split out

The script swap was attempted as part of #1167 and reverted. A test-coverage probe (`env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GITHUB_APM_PAT -u ADO_APM_PAT pytest tests/integration/`) collected 559 tests across 64 files but produced **88 failures across 12 files** — none of them caused by the marker refactor itself. The bash script silently invoked only 26 files; the other 38 have either no markers or surface real pre-existing bugs. Shipping the swap immediately would mix marker-gap noise with real-bug noise on the very first CI run, which would train maintainers to ignore integration results — exactly the failure mode that #1166 is trying to fix.

## Inventory of files needing work

**41 integration test files have no `pytestmark` and no `requires_*` marker.** Of those, the following 12 produce failures when run without tokens (full list in the test-coverage probe):

Network / token gated (need `requires_github_token` or similar marker):
- `tests/integration/test_skill_bundle_live.py` (18 failures)
- `tests/integration/test_marketplace_e2e.py`
- `tests/integration/test_azure_skills_marketplace.py` (likely `requires_ado_pat`)
- `tests/integration/test_drift_check_e2e.py`
- `tests/integration/test_drift_check.py`
- `tests/integration/test_link_rewrite_e2e.py`
- `tests/integration/test_transitive_chain_e2e.py` (3 failures)
- `tests/integration/test_intra_package_cleanup.py`

Likely real bugs surfaced (need triage, not markers):
- `tests/integration/test_virtual_package_orphan_detection.py` — `test_azure_devops_virtual_collection_not_flagged_as_orphan` returns the wrong package name shape (expected `company/my-azurecollection/copilot-instructions/collections/csharp-ddd-cleanarchitecture`, got `company/my-azurecollection/copilot-instructions-csharp-ddd-cleanarchitecture`). The bash script never invoked this file — the bug has been silent in CI.
- `tests/integration/test_local_install.py` — fixtures don't create `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and the post-#1165 target detection rejects the install.
- `tests/integration/test_local_content_audit.py`
- `tests/integration/test_policy_install_e2e.py`
- `tests/integration/test_selective_install_mcp.py`

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every `tests/integration/test_*.py` file either carries an appropriate `requires_*` marker (declared in `tests/integration/conftest.py`) or is documented in this issue as a real bug to fix separately.
2. Real bugs (the second list above) are filed as their own issues and either fixed or marked `xfail` with a tracking link before the script swap lands.
3. `scripts/test-integration.sh::run_e2e_tests()` is replaced with the architect-recommended discovery call:
   ```bash
   export APM_E2E_TESTS=1
   export APM_RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1
   pytest tests/integration/ -v -s --tb=short --ignore=tests/integration/marketplace
   ```
4. CI release validation (`build-release.yml`) passes on a token-equipped run.
5. A second probe (token-stripped) returns 0 failures — only skips driven by markers.

## Reference design

Architect-recommended approach D: full discovery + explicit `--ignore` for legacy `marketplace/`, no `KNOWN_EXCLUDED` deselect list. The script was reduced from 739 to 354 lines in the PR1 attempt; that diff is preserved in the worktree at `1c08e15f^` for reuse once gates 1-2 above are met.

## DevX nits to fold in

- Pre-run banner: `echo "Running integration tests ($(find tests/integration -name 'test_*.py' | wc -l) files, ignoring marketplace)..."` before the pytest invocation (devx-ux-expert nit).
- Drop the legacy 22-line success summary in `main()` listing "HERO SCENARIO 1/2/3..." — pytest's own summary line is the correct signal once the script orchestrates a single invocation (devx-ux-expert nit).

## Out of scope

- CI workflow changes beyond removing now-dead branches in `build-release.yml`.
- Windows `.ps1` parity.
- `tests/integration/marketplace/` (legacy fixtures kept on the old gate).

issues.title: [Feature] GitLab host support for marketplace and install
issues.body:
## Problem

GitLab does not implement GitHub's Contents API (`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/...`). Today, APM uses generic FQDN logic that assumes `/api/v3` endpoints with GitHub-compatible URL shapes, which breaks:

1. **Marketplace fetch** - `marketplace.json` cannot be retrieved from GitLab-hosted repositories
2. **File reads during install** - Single file downloads (e.g., `SKILL.md`) fail for GitLab-hosted packages
3. **Git operations** - GitLab uses different authentication conventions than GitHub for HTTPS git-over-PAT
4. **Host classification** - GitLab hosts are misclassified as "generic", causing token misrouting (GitHub tokens sent to GitLab hosts)

### Current behavior
- `apm install gitlab.com/group/project` fails with API errors or authentication failures
- GitLab PATs supplied via `GITLAB_TOKEN` are not recognized; APM attempts to use `GITHUB_TOKEN` instead
- Nested GitLab groups (e.g., `group/subgroup/repo`) are not handled correctly

## Proposed Solution

Add first-class GitLab host support with explicit host classification, GitLab REST API v4 integration, and PAT-primary HTTPS git transport.

### Key capabilities

| Capability | Implementation |
|------------|----------------|
| **Host detection** | Recognize `gitlab.com`, `GITLAB_HOST` env var, and `APM_GITLAB_HOSTS` list |
| **API integration** | Use GitLab Files API v4 for marketplace and file reads |
| **Token chain** | Support `GITLAB_APM_PAT` → `GITLAB_TOKEN` resolution (isolated from GitHub tokens) |
| **Git transport** | PAT-primary HTTPS with GitLab-compatible auth (not GitHub `x-access-token` convention) |
| **Shorthand resolution** | Probe repo boundaries left-to-right for nested group paths |

### Host classification order
```
github.com → kind="github"
*.ghe.com → kind="ghe_cloud"
Azure DevOps FQDNs → kind="ado"
GITHUB_HOST match → kind="ghes" (GHES takes precedence)
GitLab detection → kind="gitlab"
Generic FQDN → kind="generic"
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `apm install gitlab.com/group/project` succeeds using only `GITLAB_APM_PAT` or `GITLAB_TOKEN`
- [ ] GitLab SaaS (`gitlab.com`) is auto-detected without configuration
- [ ] Self-managed GitLab hosts work via `GITLAB_HOST` or `APM_GITLAB_HOSTS`
- [ ] `marketplace.json` fetch uses GitLab Files API v4 when source is GitLab-hosted
- [ ] Git operations (clone, fetch, ls-remote) succeed via PAT-primary HTTPS without external credential helpers
- [ ] `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_APM_PAT` are NOT sent to GitLab hosts
- [ ] Token-bearing URLs and errors are redacted in logs and diagnostics
- [ ] Nested group paths (e.g., `group/subgroup/repo`) resolve correctly
- [ ] Direct shorthand installs probe repo boundaries left-to-right for earliest qualifying match
- [ ] `apm deps list` shows `gitlab` as Source for GitLab-class dependencies
- [ ] All existing GitHub.com, GHES, Azure DevOps behavior remains unchanged (non-regression)
- [ ] Full pytest suite passes (`uv run pytest -q`)

## Out of Scope

- SSH as primary transport (remains optional fallback)
- GitLab CI-specific token handling (use `GITLAB_APM_PAT` in CI)
- GitLab Issue/MR integration
- GitLab-specific marketplace features beyond file fetch

## Suggested Labels

`type/feature`, `area/auth`, `area/marketplace`, `area/install`

## References

- Spec: `apm-gitlab-host-support.spec.md` (stable)
- Related work: Token precedence fix for GitLab hosts

issues.title: Support persisting CLI flags via `apm config` (e.g. `allow-protocol-fallback`, `ssh`)
issues.body:
### Problem

Several `apm install` behaviours are controlled by environment variables (e.g. `APM_ALLOW_PROTOCOL_FALLBACK=1`) or CLI flags (`--ssh`, `--allow-protocol-fallback`). These cannot be persisted via `apm config` — today the only valid config keys are `auto-integrate`, `temp-dir`, and `copilot-cowork-skills-dir`.

This creates friction for users who rely on SSH-based authentication to GitHub rather than PAT tokens. Every `apm install` invocation requires either:

1. Passing `--allow-protocol-fallback` or `--ssh` on every command, or
2. Setting `APM_ALLOW_PROTOCOL_FALLBACK=1` in a shell profile (`.zshrc`, `.bashrc`, etc.)

Neither option is ideal:

- **Windows users** (PowerShell, cmd) have a very different mechanism for persisting environment variables, making cross-platform instructions inconsistent.
- **Users who prefer not to modify rc files** have no persistent configuration path at all.
- **Teams sharing APM setups** cannot standardise transport preferences without documenting shell-specific workarounds per OS.

### Example scenario

A contributor authenticates to GitHub via SSH keys (no PAT configured). When they run:

```bash
apm install my-package@my-marketplace
```

The install fails because the default HTTPS clone cannot authenticate. The workaround is:

```bash
APM_ALLOW_PROTOCOL_FALLBACK=1 apm install my-package@my-marketplace
# or
apm install --allow-protocol-fallback my-package@my-marketplace
```

This must be repeated for every install, update, or marketplace operation. There is no way to persist this preference.

### Proposed solution

Extend `apm config set` to accept keys that mirror existing environment variables and CLI flags. For example:

```bash
# Persist protocol fallback preference
apm config set allow-protocol-fallback true

# Persist SSH transport preference
apm config set ssh true
```

Once set, these would be read automatically by all `apm` commands — no environment variable or CLI flag needed.

### Suggested scope

At minimum, the following should be configurable via `apm config`:

| Config key | Env var | CLI flag |
|---|---|---|
| `allow-protocol-fallback` | `APM_ALLOW_PROTOCOL_FALLBACK` | `--allow-protocol-fallback` |
| `ssh` | _(none)_ | `--ssh` |

More broadly, any behaviour currently controlled by an environment variable should have a corresponding `apm config` key, so the configuration surface is unified and discoverable.

### Additional context

- Current valid config keys: `auto-integrate`, `temp-dir`, `copilot-cowork-skills-dir`
- Precedence suggestion: CLI flag > env var > `apm config` > default

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-05-11
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-05-11
**APM Version**: 0.13.0 (9216516)
**Commands Inspected**: 24

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 2 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 1 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm update` documented as self-updater, but it refreshes dependencies

- **Command**: `apm update`
- **Problem**: The CLI reference docs describe `apm update` as "Update APM to the latest version" and document the `--check` flag, but the actual command refreshes APM *dependencies*. The self-update behavior lives in `apm self-update`, which has no dedicated section in `cli-commands.md`.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm update --help` output: `"Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs"` with options `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`
  - `apm self-update --help` output: `"Update the APM CLI binary itself to the latest version"` with `--check` option
  - Docs (`cli-commands.md`, line 793): `"### apm update - Update APM to the latest version"` and `"Update the APM CLI to the latest version available on GitHub releases."`
  - Runtime confirmation: `apm update --check` prints `"[!] 'apm update --check' is the deprecated self-updater shim. Use 'apm update --dry-run' to preview dependency changes, or 'apm self-update --check'"`
- **Suggested Fix**: Rename the docs section to `apm update - Refresh APM dependencies` with the correct options (`--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`). Add a separate `apm self-update` section documenting `--check`. Update all examples accordingly.

#### `apm config list` does not exist

- **Command**: `apm config list`
- **Problem**: `apm config list` is listed as a command to inspect in the CLI checker, and is a natural command to expect given `apm config get/set/unset`, but running it returns an error.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm config list --help` output: `"Error: No such command 'list'."`
  - `apm config --help` lists only: `get`, `set`, `unset`
  - `apm config` (no subcommand) correctly shows all configuration values as a table.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `apm config list` as an alias that calls `apm config` (the default show-all-config behavior), or explicitly document that `apm config` with no subcommand is the equivalent of `list`. Update any tooling or documentation that references `apm config list`.

---

### Medium Severity

#### Docs describe `apm update --check` without noting deprecation

- **Command**: `apm update --check`
- **Problem**: The docs show `apm update --check` as a valid way to check for a new CLI version with no deprecation notice, but at runtime the command prints a deprecation warning.
- **Evidence**:
  - Docs (`cli-commands.md`, line 807): `"# Check if an update is available\napm update --check"`
  - CLI output when run: `"[!] 'apm update --check' is the deprecated self-updater shim. Use 'apm update --dry-run' to preview dependency changes, or 'apm self-update --check' to check for a new CLI binary. Forwarding for back-compat (deprecated)."`
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace the `apm update --check` example with `apm self-update --check` and add a note: "`apm update --check` is deprecated and forwards to the self-update shim for back-compat."

#### `apm config` output uses Unicode box-drawing characters, violating ASCII encoding policy

- **Command**: `apm config` (no subcommand)
- **Problem**: Running `apm config` displays a rich table with Unicode box-drawing characters. The repo's `.github/instructions` encoding policy requires all CLI output to stay within printable ASCII (U+0020-U+007E) to avoid `UnicodeEncodeError` on Windows cp1252 terminals.
- **Evidence**: Running `apm config` outputs:
  ```
  +- Current APM Configuration -+
  (actual output uses Unicode: U+250F, U+2501, U+2513, U+2521, U+2529, U+2502, U+2503)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Render the configuration table using ASCII-only characters (e.g., `+---+---+` borders), or use the plain-text `[key]: value` format consistent with the project's `STATUS_SYMBOLS` convention in `src/apm_cli/utils/console.py`.

---

### Low Severity

#### Version warning example in docs uses emoji character

- **Location**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md`, line 827
- **Problem**: The docs show a version-check notification using the `warning sign` emoji character, which violates the repo's ASCII encoding policy (scope includes documentation markdown files).
- **Evidence**: Line 827 in `cli-commands.md` contains a warning emoji followed by `"A new version of APM is available: 0.7.0 (current: 0.6.3)"`
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace the warning emoji with `[!]` per the `STATUS_SYMBOLS` convention documented in the encoding rules.

---

### Clean Areas

- `apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm compile`, `apm run`: help text is clear, consistent, and well-structured.
- `apm deps list/tree/info/clean/update`: all subcommands present with consistent help text.
- `apm mcp search/show/install`: all present and coherent; `mcp install` correctly self-documents as an alias for `apm install --mcp`.
- `apm config set/get/unset`: work correctly with proper missing-argument error messages.
- `apm runtime setup`: well-documented with correct enum constraints for the runtime argument.
- Error handling: invalid flags and missing required arguments produce clean, actionable error messages with no stack traces on all tested commands.
- `--help` and `-h` work on all tested commands and subcommands.
- `--dry-run` is consistently named (not `--dryrun`) across all commands that support it.
- `--yes`/`-y` is consistently present on commands that perform destructive or irreversible operations (`apm update`, `apm deps clean`).

issues.title: [FEATURE] First-party apm-authoring package with conventions for APM authors
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
APM defines the primitive types but doesn't ship guidance on how to author a good package. New authors keep rediscovering the same rules: instruction vs skill, `applyTo:` scope, trigger phrasing, what to leave out, version policy, layout. The result is uneven quality across the ecosystem.

The cleanest fix is the one APM is already optimised for: an APM package whose rules auto-activate exactly when an author is editing an APM primitive.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A first-party `apm-authoring` package distributed from this repo:

- instructions file scoped to `apm.yml`, `SKILL.md`, `*.instructions.md`, `*.prompt.md`, `*.agent.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`;
- one `SKILL.md` covering package layout, the instruction-vs-skill decision, frontmatter rules, version policy, and common pitfalls.

Installed as a `devDependency`, it would steer any APM-aware agent the moment someone opens a `SKILL.md` or `apm.yml` — no separate docs trip needed.

We have a working version we'd be glad to upstream as a starting point:
https://github.com/Netcracker/qubership-ai-packages/tree/main/agent-packages/apm-authoring

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Each org maintains its own authoring skill (current state — causes ecosystem drift).
- Static authoring docs in the README — doesn't activate at the moment of authoring, which is APM's whole value proposition.
- An `apm lint` validator — useful and complementary, but only catches schema-level mistakes, not "this should be a skill, not an instruction" decisions.

**Additional context**
Happy to contribute the package itself, a vendor-neutral rewrite, or just the conventions list — whatever fits the repo's direction.
Also happy to discuss whether the right home is in-tree, a sibling `microsoft/apm-authoring` repo, or a community-maintained package.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Progressive test coverage gates (strangler-fig ratchet)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
There is no coverage measurement or gating in CI today. We have no
visibility into coverage trends, and regressions can land silently.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Introduce test coverage gates to CI using a strangler-fig ratchet pattern.
Start with observability, then progressively tighten thresholds across
4 phases until we reach steady-state targets of **80% unit / 70% integration**.

### Baselines (measured locally)

| Tier | Baseline | Steady-state target |
|------|----------|---------------------|
| Unit | 80% | 80% |
| Integration | 49% | 70% |

### Phase plan

| Phase | Unit gate | Integration gate | Intent |
|-------|-----------|------------------|--------|
| 1 | Report only | Report only | Observability |
| 2 | 75% fail | Report only | First unit gate |
| 3 | 80% fail | 55% fail | Both tiers gated |
| 4 (steady) | 80% fail | 70% fail | Steady state |

### Ratchet rule

After each phase, if actual coverage exceeds the gate by 5+ points,
raise the gate to `actual - 3`. This prevents regression while allowing
normal fluctuation.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Hard-gating at 80%/70% from day one -- rejected because the 49%
  integration baseline would block all PRs until gap-fill is done.
- No gates, report only -- rejected because reports alone do not
  prevent regressions.

**Additional context**
Sub-issues track each phase:

- [ ] #1399 -- Phase 1: Coverage observability
- [ ] #1401 -- Phase 2: Unit 75% gate
- [ ] #1402 -- Phase 3: Unit 80% / Integration 55%
- [ ] #1400 -- Phase 4: Steady-state 80% / 70%

issues.title: [BUG] `compilation.strategy` defaulting to `distributed` is unintuitive, under-documented
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

In initializing a new, fairly empty repo, I set up `apm` with some rules I know I'd use in fleshing things out. At the time, I had only one shell script in the repo, in a `scripts/` folder, and was going to continue things.

I added my various instructions for things like shell scripts, TypeScript, etc., to `apm.yml` and did install/compile.

I was not expecting it, but **suddenly `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` showed up in my `scripts/` folder.**

This is currently only documented in two somewhat out-of-the-way places:

1. [In the `apm compile` docs, as a small note.](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/ef74bddc1a9403ad69ced20be1969a21784afd45/docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/compile.md?plain=1#L199)
2. [In the manifest schema docs, noting the configuration setting.](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/ef74bddc1a9403ad69ced20be1969a21784afd45/docs/src/content/docs/reference/manifest-schema.md?plain=1#L517)

I haven't seen this before because I've always added `apm` to existing, larger repos that wouldn't necessarily cause this distribution to occur.

Note this also somewhat overlaps with #1138 (use of `.claude/rules/` over including instructions right in `CLAUDE.md`) and #1445 (`compilation.strategy` is ignored for `CLAUDE.md` generation).

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create some instructions for shell scripts with frontmatter `applyTo: *.sh`
2. Create some instructions for markdown with frontmatter `applyTo: *.md`
3. Add an `apm.yml` that includes both instructions. Add targets for `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`.
5. Create a folder `scripts/` and put a shell script in there.
6. `apm install`
7. `apm compile`

You will end up with:

```text
.
|-.claude/
|  +-rules/
|    +-markdown.md
|    +-shell.md
|-.github/
|  +-instructions/
|    +-markdown.instructions.md
|    +-shell.instructions.md
|-scripts/
|  +-AGENTS.md # has the *.sh instructions
|  +-CLAUDE.md # has the *.sh instructions
|-AGENTS.md # has the *.md instructions
|-CLAUDE.md # has the *.md instructions
```

This was unexpected because it was a brand new repo I was in the process of working through. I wouldn't expect the output of `apm compile` to change where various generated files are. Assuming that's intentional, it also seems that `apm compile` should have `--clean` on _by default_ (or perhaps act based on `compilation.strategy`) because I can't imagine a time where you _wouldn't_ want to clean up orphaned distributed files.

(Again, this ties to #1445 - `apm compile --clean` doesn't actually clean up orphaned CLAUDE.md files at the moment, which added to the confusion here.)

**Expected behavior**

I expect:

- **Documentation in more places that touch on this**, like maybe ["Primitives and Targets"](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/concepts/primitives-and-targets.md) since that speaks to the outputs.
- **Consistency across commands and the lifecycle.** If it's running in distributed mode, both `apm install` and `apm compile` should default to managing things in a distributed lifecycle; if it's running in single-file mode, both `apm install` and `apm compile` should behave as such. I shouldn't have to "know" to run with `--clean` when I'm in one lifecycle and not the other. The inconsistency is a UX surprise.
- **Deduplication of instructions.** If it's in `.claude/rules` it doesn't make sense to also put it _conditionally_ in `CLAUDE.md`. If it's in `.github/instructions` for Copilot, it doesn't make sense to duplicate it in `AGENTS.md`. (Or, should you choose, always put it in `AGENTS.md` and _don't_ put it in `.github/instructions`.) If the principle this behavior is going for is "minimal context" then it's failing on the grounds of the duplication.

---

I'm not entirely sure how this should be fixed or I'd submit PRs for it. It seems like unifying the behavior of the CLI across lifecycle may be a somewhat breaking change. Once the deduplication happens (if it happens?) it seems like the documentation would change, so based on #1138 I'm not sure what to document.

If the team here can provide some guidance, I'd be 100% happy to contribute to the solution.

#### `apm targets` synopsis misleadingly shows `COMMAND [ARGS]...`

- **Command**: `apm targets --help`
- **Problem**: The usage line reads `apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`, which implies `targets` is a command group requiring a subcommand. In reality `apm targets` runs directly with no subcommands and outputs a table of resolved targets. No subcommands are listed in the help. Users following the usage line would incorrectly expect to supply a subcommand.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Show resolved targets for the current project. If APM detects a target you
    don't intend...

  Options:
    --json  Output as JSON instead of a table.
    --all   Include the agent-skills meta-target in JSON output...
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Running `apm targets` (no args) produces the expected table output with no error, confirming it is a standalone command, not a group.
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the usage synopsis to `apm targets [OPTIONS]` (remove `COMMAND [ARGS]...`). If this is a Click `Group` used as a default command, switch to `@click.command` or add `invoke_without_command=True` with a corrected usage string.

---

#### `apm config list` subcommand is absent, breaking the group subcommand naming convention

- **Command**: `apm config list --help`
- **Problem**: Every other multi-subcommand group in APM exposes a `list` subcommand (`apm deps list`, `apm mcp list`, `apm runtime list`, `apm marketplace list`, `apm experimental list`). `apm config` breaks this pattern -- it has no `list` subcommand. Running `apm config list --help` returns an error:
  ```
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
  Try 'apm config --help' for help.

  Error: No such command 'list'.
  ```
  The equivalent functionality (show all config keys) exists via `apm config get` (no argument) or `apm config` (no subcommand), but neither matches the established `list` naming pattern. Users familiar with other groups will attempt `apm config list` and hit this error.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `apm config list` as an alias or distinct subcommand that outputs the same table as `apm config get` (no args). The `apm config` docs already describe this output under "With no subcommand" -- a `list` subcommand would simply expose it via the standard naming.

---

#### `apm mcp install --help` renders options as inline prose rather than standard Click option blocks

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: Unlike every other command in the CLI, `apm mcp install --help` does not render its options as a structured Click option table. Instead, common options are listed as a single unformatted prose block at the bottom of the help text:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  This is inconsistent with every other command's help output, making it harder to read, and the line-wrapping breaks the option names across lines (e.g. `--dry-` and `run` appear on separate lines). Users cannot tab-complete or discover default values from this help block.
- **Suggested Fix**: Since `apm mcp install` is an alias for `apm install --mcp`, either (a) forward the full `apm install` option definitions to `apm mcp install` so Click renders them normally, or (b) document the forwarding clearly and point users to `apm install --mcp --help` as the canonical reference -- but keep the `Options:` section clean.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm prune` is missing a `--yes` / `-y` confirmation bypass flag

- **Command**: `apm prune --help`
- **Problem**: `apm prune` removes packages not listed in `apm.yml`, which is a destructive operation. It exposes `--dry-run` but no `-y`/`--yes` to skip interactive confirmation. Every other destructive command in the CLI provides this flag: `apm deps clean` has `--yes`, `apm runtime remove` has `--yes`, `apm uninstall` is non-interactive by default. The inconsistency makes it harder to use `apm prune` safely in CI scripts.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm prune [OPTIONS]

    Remove APM packages not listed in apm.yml

  Options:
    --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
    --help     Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-y, --yes` to `apm prune` with the same semantics as `apm deps clean --yes`: skip the confirmation prompt (for CI and scripts).

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no inconsistencies found:

- **Error handling**: All tested invalid-argument scenarios (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no PACKAGE, `apm config set` with no KEY) produced clean, actionable error messages with no stack traces.
- **`apm init`**, **`apm install`**, **`apm uninstall`**, **`apm update`**, **`apm compile`**, **`apm run`**: Core commands have consistent flag naming (`--dry-run`, `--verbose`/`-v`, `--target`/`-t`, `--yes`/`-y`, `--global`/`-g`) and clear descriptions.
- **`apm deps` group** (`list`, `tree`, `info`, `update`, `clean`): All subcommands present, consistent with `docs/reference/cli/deps.md`.
- **`apm mcp` group** (`list`, `search`, `show`, `install`): Subcommands present and consistent with `docs/reference/cli/mcp.md`. Default values match (`--limit 20` for `list`, `--limit 10` for `search`).
- **`apm config`** (`get`, `set`, `unset`): Documented subcommands exist and function correctly. Docs accurately reflect available keys and behavior.
- **`apm runtime`** (`setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove`): All four subcommands exist and match `docs/reference/cli/runtime.md`. Flag `-y`/`--yes` on `remove` is consistent.
- **Documentation cross-reference**: CLI reference docs at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` accurately reflect the CLI surface for all checked commands. No documented command was found missing from the CLI, and no undocumented top-level command was found in the CLI that is missing a reference page.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works on every tested command and subcommand.
- **ASCII output compliance**: All help text stays within printable ASCII; no Unicode box-drawing or emoji in help strings.

issues.title: feat(pack): --create-tag and --push flags to create and push release tag after --check-versions
issues.body:
## Summary

Add `--create-tag` and `--push` flags to `apm pack`. When
`--check-versions` succeeds, `--create-tag` creates the git tag the
check is verifying (e.g. `v1.2.0` for lockstep marketplaces, or one
per package for `per_package`). `--push` follows up by pushing the
created tag to the configured remote. Refuses to operate on a dirty
working tree, on existing tags, or when the manifest version and the
tag-to-create disagree.

## Motivation

The current release dance for a marketplace looks like this:

1. Bump `marketplace.yml` version.
2. `apm pack --check-versions --check-clean` (release gates).
3. Inspect output.
4. `git tag v1.2.0`.
5. `git push origin v1.2.0`.
6. Wait for the marketplace consumers to pick up the new tag.

Steps 4 and 5 are mechanical and error-prone: tag-name typos, forgotten
push, or pushing the wrong commit (e.g. when the local HEAD has
unrelated drift from `origin/main`). The proposal folds the mechanical
steps into the gated command itself, so the release is one invocation
instead of three, and any failure unwinds cleanly.

## Proposal

Two new flags on `apm pack`:

- `--create-tag` — after `--check-versions` succeeds, create the git
  tag(s) implied by the marketplace's versioning strategy:
  - `lockstep`: one tag `v{marketplace_version}`.
  - `tag_pattern`: one tag per package using the configured pattern.
  - `per_package`: one tag per package using `{name}--v{version}`
    (Claude Code / PR #1422 convention).

  Tag creation is annotated (`git tag -a -m "Release v1.2.0"`) and
  signed if `tag.gpgSign` is set in git config.

- `--push` — after creating tags, push them to the remote inferred
  from `git config branch.<current>.remote` (default `origin`). Only
  pushes the newly created tags; never pushes branches.

Both flags require `--check-versions` to also be set (the version
agreement check is the gate that justifies tag creation).
`--push` may be used with or without `--create-tag`, but without
`--create-tag` it errors out (no tag was made; nothing to push).

Refusal conditions (all exit code 1, distinct messages):

1. Working tree is dirty.
2. Tag(s) already exist locally or on the remote.
3. Manifest's marketplace version disagrees with the tag-to-create.
4. No git remote configured.
5. `--check-versions` not passed.

## Examples

One-shot release:

```bash
apm pack --check-versions --check-clean --create-tag --push
```

Inspection (dry-run; reports tags that would be created and pushed,
makes no git calls):

```bash
apm pack --check-versions --create-tag --push --dry-run
```

Tag locally, push manually later:

```bash
apm pack --check-versions --create-tag
git push origin --tags
```

## Considerations

- Composes with `--check-clean`: when both gates run and both pass,
  tag creation runs.
- Composes with `--dry-run`: dry-run never invokes git.
- Composes with `--json`: success/failure of tag creation and push
  are added to the existing JSON output envelope under
  `tag_creation` and `tag_push` keys.
- The flag pair refuses to run if `apm pack` is operating in
  bundle-only mode (no `marketplace:` block) — tag-on-bundle has no
  natural single-version source.

## Out of scope

- Releasing to a non-origin remote via flag. Use `git config` first.
- GPG configuration help; users wire their own gpgSign.
- Creating tags via the GitHub API instead of `git push` — keeps the
  command's only side effect inside the local git repo + the user's
  configured remote.
- Per-package tag-pattern overrides surfaced via flag; those already
  live in `marketplace.yml` under `tagPattern`.

## References

- Existing release gates: `apm pack --check-versions` (exit code 3),
  `--check-clean` (exit code 4).
- Versioning strategies: `lockstep`, `tag_pattern`, `per_package`
  (`marketplace.versioning.strategy`).
- Authoring repo mode discussion: #1474.

## Related (same surface, orthogonal problems)

- #1381 — `apm pack --check-clean` error message rewrite. Same
  command family, different feature (error UX vs. new flags). Land
  independently; both improve the release flow.
- #1474 — Authoring-repo mode (`self_install: false` on `apm pack`).
  Operates at install time (which files get deployed) while this
  issue operates at pack time (tag creation). Complementary,
  stackable, no conflict.

issues.title: apm install: targets: (plural) leaks copilot deploy when target: (singular) absent
issues.body:
## Summary

When `apm.yml` declares targets only via the plural `targets:` field (no singular `target:`), `apm install` deploys to **both** the configured target(s) **and** to `copilot` (`.github/`). The log line correctly reports the resolved set, but the deploy phase ignores it.

Reproduced on **v0.15.0** (also present on `main` at the time of writing).

## Repro

`apm.yml`:

```yaml
name: example
version: 0.1.0
targets:
  - claude
dependencies:
  apm:
    - somostuio/coding-agents-config/packages/core
```

`apm install` output:

```
[i] Targets: claude  (source: apm.yml)
  [+] github.com/somostuio/coding-agents-config/packages/core @1de9bcca
  |-- 6 prompts adopted -> .github/prompts/
  |-- 8 agents integrated -> .claude/agents/, .github/agents/
  |-- 6 commands integrated -> .claude/commands/
  |-- 7 instruction(s) integrated (7 adopted) -> .claude/rules/, .github/instructions/
  |-- Skill integrated -> .agents/skills/, .claude/skills/
```

Provenance line says `Targets: claude (source: apm.yml)`, but `.github/{agents,instructions,prompts}/` are created and populated. The lockfile records both target trees as `deployed_files`.

## Expected

With `targets: [claude]` (and no `--target` CLI override), only the `claude` profile should be deployed — equivalent behavior to `target: claude` (singular) or `--target claude`.

## Root cause

`src/apm_cli/install/phases/targets.py:117` reads only the singular attribute:

```python
config_target = ctx.apm_package.target

_explicit = ctx.target_override or config_target or None
```

`ApmPackage` (see `src/apm_cli/models/apm_package.py:230-237`) stores `target` (singular) and `targets` (plural) as separate fields. With only `targets:` declared, `apm_package.target` is `None`, so `_explicit` is `None` for the **legacy** resolver call at `:144`.

The legacy resolver (`src/apm_cli/integration/targets.py:825-898`) with `explicit_target=None` skips branch 1 (explicit), runs branch 2 (auto-detect by directory presence), and on a clean workspace falls through to branch 3 — the hard-coded `[copilot]` fallback at line 898.

Meanwhile the v2 path (`install/phases/targets.py:303-309`) correctly reads both keys via `_read_yaml_targets` → `parse_targets_field`, so v2 returns `[claude]`.

The merge at `install/phases/targets.py:399-404`:

```python
_v2_names = {t.name for t in _v2_targets}          # {'claude'}
_legacy_only = [t for t in _targets if t.name not in _v2_names]  # [copilot]
_targets = _v2_targets + _legacy_only              # [claude, copilot]
```

…re-injects the legacy copilot fallback into the final deploy set. The downstream integrators then deploy to both. The "Targets: claude (source: apm.yml)" log is emitted from v2 provenance only and never reflects this re-injection.

## Suggested fix

Make the legacy resolver see the same explicit input as v2. Smallest change at `install/phases/targets.py:117`:

```python
config_target = ctx.apm_package.target or ctx.apm_package.targets
```

Alternative: drop the unconditional copilot fallback from the legacy path when v2 has already resolved a non-empty target set, or refuse to merge legacy auto-detect results when an apm.yml-declared target intent exists.

## Workaround for users

Use the singular form in `apm.yml` until fixed:

```yaml
target: claude
```

CSV / list forms (`target: claude,cursor` or `target: [claude]`) also work because `parse_target_field` handles them.

## Environment

- apm 0.15.0 (1b2c0f0)
- macOS arm64 (Darwin 24.4.0)

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-05-28
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-05-28
**APM Version**: 0.16.0 (e94af4a)
**Commands Inspected**: 44

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 3 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm targets` Usage line claims subcommands but has none

- **Command**: `apm targets`
- **Problem**: The usage line reads `Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...` — the `COMMAND [ARGS]...` placeholder implies subcommands exist, but the help lists no commands at all. The command functions as a standalone (invoke-without-command group), so the `COMMAND [ARGS]...` fragment is misleading and will confuse users who try to pass a subcommand.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Show resolved targets for the current project. If APM detects a target you
    don't intend (e.g. CLAUDE.md is documentation, not a Claude Code config),
    pin your targets explicitly in apm.yml.

  Options:
    --json  Output as JSON instead of a table.
    --all   Include the agent-skills meta-target in JSON output (excluded by default).
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  No `Commands:` section follows.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either convert `apm targets` from a Click group to a plain `@click.command()` (removing the misleading `COMMAND [ARGS]...` fragment), or add at least one real subcommand if future sub-actions are planned. The simplest fix is `@click.command` instead of `@click.group(invoke_without_command=True)`.

---

#### `apm mcp install --help` renders common options as an unreadable prose blob

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: The help text shows "common options" as a single wrapped paragraph rather than structured `--flag  description` lines. Users cannot quickly scan what flags are available.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) forward all relevant options from `apm install --mcp` into `apm mcp install` so they appear as proper Click options, or (b) replace the prose blob with a clean, newline-separated option summary. Option (a) matches how Click-based CLIs normally expose aliases.

---

#### `apm deps why` examples section is badly formatted in help text

- **Command**: `apm deps why`
- **Problem**: The `Examples:` block in the command description runs all examples together on a single wrapped line with no visual separation, making them hard to read.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm deps why [OPTIONS] PACKAGE

    Explain why a package is installed by walking the lockfile back to one or
    more direct dependencies that pulled it in.

    Examples:   apm deps why shared-utils   apm deps why acme-org/shared-utils
    --json   apm deps why shared-utils --global
  ```
  Each example should appear on its own line.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add explicit newlines (`\n`) between examples in the docstring so Click renders them as separate lines, e.g.:
  ```
  Examples:\n
    apm deps why shared-utils\n
    apm deps why acme-org/shared-utils --json\n
    apm deps why shared-utils --global
  ```

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm prune` missing `--verbose` flag, inconsistent with sibling commands

- **Command**: `apm prune`
- **Problem**: `apm uninstall` (which also removes packages) exposes `-v, --verbose` for detailed removal info. `apm prune` does not.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm uninstall --help`: shows `  -v, --verbose  Show detailed removal information`
  - `apm prune --help`: only shows `  --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing` and `  --help`
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-v, --verbose  Show detailed removal information` to `apm prune`, consistent with `apm uninstall`.

---

#### `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, and `apm deps info` lack `--verbose`, while `apm deps update` has it

- **Command**: `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, `apm deps info`
- **Problem**: Within the same `apm deps` command group, `apm deps update` exposes `-v, --verbose`, but the inspection/read subcommands (`list`, `tree`, `info`) do not. This is an inconsistency — users who want more detail on listed or tree-displayed deps have no flag for it.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm deps update --help`: shows `  -v, --verbose  Show detailed update information`
  - `apm deps list --help`: no verbose flag
  - `apm deps tree --help`: no verbose flag
  - `apm deps info --help`: no verbose flag
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-v, --verbose` to `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, and `apm deps info` to surface additional detail (e.g., resolved refs, file counts, source URLs) when requested.

---

#### `apm install` `--update` deprecation notice is very long and easy to miss

- **Command**: `apm install`
- **Problem**: The deprecation notice for `--update` is buried in the middle of the option description and spans multiple lines, making it hard to spot at a glance. The description also conflates two separate concerns (what `--update` does vs. what to use instead) in one long sentence.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
    --update  Update dependencies to latest Git references
              (deprecated: prefer 'apm update' for an interactive plan, or 'apm
              update --yes' for CI). Unlike --refresh, --update restructures the
              entire dependency graph.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Prefix the deprecation with a clear `[DEPRECATED]` marker and separate the migration hint from the behavioral description:
  ```
    --update  [DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead] Update dependencies to
              latest Git references. Unlike --refresh, restructures the entire
              dependency graph.
  ```

---

### Clean Areas

- All documented commands exist and are reachable in the CLI (no doc/CLI drift found).
- Error messages for invalid flags and missing required arguments are clear and consistent (no stack traces on bad input).
- `--help` / `-h` works on every tested command and subcommand.
- `--dry-run` naming is consistent wherever it appears (`apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm deps clean`, `apm compile`, `apm pack`, `apm prune`, `apm audit`, `apm unpack`).
- `--global` / `-g` naming is consistent across `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, `apm deps update`, `apm view`, `apm outdated`.
- `--target` / `-t` is consistent across `apm install`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm deps update`.
- `--verbose` / `-v` short flag is consistent wherever `--verbose` appears.
- `apm config`, `apm cache`, `apm runtime`, `apm mcp`, `apm marketplace`, `apm experimental`, `apm plugin`, `apm policy` subcommand groupings are clean and consistently structured.
- `apm self-update`, `apm search`, `apm view`, `apm outdated`, `apm publish`, `apm pack`, `apm audit` options are well-formed and match their respective documentation pages.
