issues.title: [FEATURE] Machine-level, root-owned config to enforce registry-only installs (non-overridable by users)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

There is currently no way for an enterprise to enforce, at the machine level, that packages may only be installed from an approved internal registry. Today APM can resolve packages two ways: directly from a git host (for example a public `git clone` from github.com, which needs [zero setup](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/consumer/authentication/#the-30-second-answer)), or through a registry ([a private/self-hosted registry such as Artifactory or JFrog](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/registries/#2-install-from-a-private-or-self-hosted-registry), including JFrog's official [Agent Packages Repositories](https://docs.jfrog.com/artifactory/docs/agent-packages-repositories)).

When a user is signed in to GitHub, APM also discovers and applies policy from the org's `.github` repo, so governance kicks in. But that discovery is GitHub-specific, and on other remotes (or when discovery doesn't fire) [no policy is applied at install time](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/enterprise/governance-guide/#14-known-gaps-and-limitations). Since public github.com needs [no credentials at all](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/consumer/authentication/#the-30-second-answer), an unauthenticated user can still clone straight from it with nothing gating the install. That makes the policy path effectively opt-in.

The deeper problem is that every existing control point is user-writable:

- CLI config lives only at [`~/.apm/config.json`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/config/#configuration-file), the user-level file this command reads and writes.
- The documented [resolution order](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/config/#resolution-order) is environment variable, then `~/.apm/config.json`, then the built-in default. Environment variables win, and the user controls both.
- Registry resolution follows [precedence chains](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/registries/#precedence-chains) across `apm-policy.yml`, the project `apm.yml`, the workspace `~/.apm/apm.yml`, and `~/.apm/config.json` — every layer of which is writable by the user or committed in a repo the user controls.

So an administrator has no tamper-resistant place to say "on this machine, only install from our internal registry, and never clone directly from a public git host." Anyone can set an env var, edit `~/.apm/config.json`, or adjust the project manifest to route around it.

I checked the source before filing this to confirm there is no existing root-owned or system-level config file: `CONFIG_DIR`/`CONFIG_FILE` in `config.py` point only at `~/.apm`, and the registry precedence chain in `deps/registry/config_loader.py` has no machine-wide layer.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a machine-level configuration file that can be owned by root (or a privileged admin group) and that users cannot overwrite, sitting at the top of the [precedence chain](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/registries/#precedence-chains) above environment variables and all user-writable config.

Rough shape:

- A well-known system path per platform, for example `/etc/apm/config.yml` on Linux/macOS and the equivalent under `ProgramData` on Windows.
- APM only trusts the file if it is owned by root/admin and not writable by the current user. If a user-owned file is dropped at that path, it is ignored (fail closed, not fail open).
- When present, it can mandate [registry definitions](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/registries/#2-install-from-a-private-or-self-hosted-registry) and pin the allowed install sources: force installs through a named internal registry, and disable direct git-host cloning.
- Highest precedence and non-overridable. Settings here cannot be relaxed by `APM_*` environment variables or by any user-writable layer in the current [resolution order](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/config/#resolution-order). It can only tighten, never loosen.
- Applies regardless of GitHub sign-in state, closing the [known install-time policy gap](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/enterprise/governance-guide/#14-known-gaps-and-limitations).

The intent is that as JFrog rolls out official registry support through their platform ([Agent Packages Repositories](https://docs.jfrog.com/artifactory/docs/agent-packages-repositories)) and APM, an organization can make that internal registry the only way packages are pulled, and enforce it with a control that lives outside the user's reach.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Environment variables (`APM_*`).** Rejected. The user owns their environment, and env vars are currently the highest-precedence layer in the [resolution order](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/config/#resolution-order), which is backwards for enforcement.
- **`~/.apm/config.json` or `~/.apm/apm.yml`.** Rejected. Both are [user-level files](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/config/#configuration-file) in the user's home directory, so they can't bind the user.
- **Repo-committed `apm-policy.yml` plus GitHub-based auto-discovery.** Helps when signed in to GitHub, but does nothing in the [documented gap](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/enterprise/governance-guide/#14-known-gaps-and-limitations) where discovery doesn't apply, and the policy file lives in a repo rather than on the locked-down machine. Related work in #1925 adds install-time policy for non-GitHub remotes via a `--policy` flag, but that is still user-invoked and file-based, not a root-owned machine mandate, so it doesn't close this gap.
- **Baking policy into a custom install image.** Doesn't generalize across teams or machines and is painful to update.

**Additional context**

- Confirmed against the current source: config is user-level only (`~/.apm/config.json`, created `0o600`), and the [registry precedence chain](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/registries/#precedence-chains) (`apm-policy.yml` > project `apm.yml` > `~/.apm/apm.yml` > `~/.apm/config.json`) has no machine-wide, root-owned layer.
- Key requirement: enforcement must come from a file the user cannot write. Ownership and permission checks (root/admin-owned, not user-writable) should gate whether the file is honored.
- Related but distinct: #1925 (install-time policy enforcement on non-GitHub remotes).

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-08-06
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-06
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (3aa0365)
**Commands Inspected**: 51 (33 top-level + 6 `deps` + 4 `mcp` + 4 `config` + 4 `runtime`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

None found. All CLI commands are present and match documentation. Error handling for invalid arguments produces clean error messages (no stack traces).

---

### Medium Severity

#### 1. Inconsistent deprecation style across commands

- **Commands**: `apm deps`, `apm init`
- **Problem**: `apm deps --help` displays `deps update` as `DEPRECATED:` (all-caps prefix), while `apm init --help` shows the deprecated `--plugin` and `--marketplace` flags as `(deprecated)` (lowercase, in parentheses). These are two different visual conventions for the same concept in the same CLI.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm deps --help (Commands section):
  update  DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset).

  # apm init --help (Options section):
  --plugin         (deprecated) Use 'apm plugin init' instead. Scaffolds plugin.json + apm.yml.
  --marketplace    (deprecated) Use 'apm marketplace init' instead. Seeds a marketplace block.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Adopt a single convention. The lowercase parenthetical `(deprecated)` style used in `apm init` is the more common Click/Typer pattern and reads more naturally in command listings. Update the `deps update` description to use the same style: `(deprecated) use 'apm update' instead (strict superset).`

---

#### 2. Inconsistent `--yes` / `-y` flag descriptions

- **Commands**: `apm update`, `apm deps clean`, `apm init`
- **Problem**: All three commands expose `-y, --yes` for the same purpose (skip a confirmation prompt), but describe it with different wording and varying detail levels.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm update
  -y, --yes    Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)

  # apm deps clean
  -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt

  # apm init
  -y, --yes    Skip interactive prompts and use auto-detected defaults
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize to a single description. Suggested canonical form: `Skip the confirmation prompt`. Add `(for CI / automation)` only where non-interactive use is specifically important (e.g. `apm update`).

---

#### 3. Inconsistent `--verbose` / `-v` flag descriptions

- **Commands**: Multiple
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` flag carries different descriptions across commands, ranging from the generic two-word form to detailed multi-clause sentences.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # Generic (run, init, mcp search, mcp show):
  -v, --verbose    Show detailed output

  # Command-specific (install):
  -v, --verbose    Show detailed installation information

  # Command-specific (uninstall):
  -v, --verbose    Show detailed removal information

  # Long-form (update):
  -v, --verbose    Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Use `Show detailed output` as the baseline. Where the command-specific meaning genuinely differs (e.g. `update`), keep the richer description. Standardize the remaining commands that use distinct but equivalent phrasings (`install`, `uninstall`) to `Show detailed output`.

---

### Low Severity

#### 4. `apm config set`, `config get`, and `config list` have no examples in help text

- **Commands**: `apm config set`, `apm config get`, `apm config list`
- **Problem**: These three subcommands display only a one-line description with no examples, accepted key names, or valid value hints. In contrast, `apm mcp install --help` shows examples inline, and the docs (`apm config` reference page) document a rich set of keys. A user running `apm config set --help` gets no guidance on what keys exist.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm config set [OPTIONS] KEY VALUE

    Set a configuration value

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add at least one example and a note pointing to valid keys. Example addition:
  ```
  Examples:
    apm config set target copilot
    apm config set self-update.channel prerelease
  Run 'apm config list' to see current values and available keys.
  ```

---

#### 5. `apm deps update` missing `--dry-run` flag

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: `apm deps update` is a write operation (refreshes dependency refs) but lacks a `--dry-run` flag. All peer write commands (`apm update`, `apm install`, `apm compile`, `apm deps clean`) expose `--dry-run`. While `deps update` is deprecated, users still running it cannot preview changes safely without it.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm deps update --help Options section -- no --dry-run present
  Options:
    -v, --verbose                 Show detailed update information
    --force                       Overwrite locally-authored files on collision
    -t, --target TARGET           Target platform (comma-separated). ...
    --parallel-downloads INTEGER  ...
    -g, --global                  Update user-scope dependencies (~/.apm/)
    --legacy-skill-paths          ...
    --help                        Show this message and exit.

  # All other write commands have:
  --dry-run    (various descriptions)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `--dry-run` to `deps update` so deprecated users can preview before migrating. Alternatively, add a note in `deps update --help` pointing to `apm update --dry-run` as the safe alternative.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all consistency checks:

- **Command/doc parity**: All 33 top-level CLI commands have a matching reference page under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. No documented command is missing from the CLI; no CLI command is missing from the docs.
- **Error handling**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (missing arg), and `apm config set` (missing args) all produce clean, actionable error messages with usage hints -- no stack traces or crashes.
- **`--help` flag**: Works correctly on every inspected command and subcommand.
- **`--global` / `-g` flag**: Present and consistently described across all commands that support it (`install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps list`, `deps tree`, `deps update`).
- **`--dry-run` flag**: Present and consistent across `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, and `deps clean`.
- **Runtime subcommands**: `list`, `setup`, `status`, `remove` -- all documented and all functional.
- **MCP subcommands**: `list`, `search`, `show`, `install` -- all documented and consistent. Default limits match docs (`list`: 20, `search`: 10).
- **Typos / grammar**: No spelling errors found in inspected help text.
- **Deprecation notices** (content): Deprecated commands and flags consistently redirect users to the correct replacement command.

issues.title: Subpath guard false-positives on a GitLab subgroup legitimately named `collections`
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm pack` rejects a perfectly valid GitLab repository URL because one of the
**subgroup** names happens to match a reserved APM primitive directory name.

Our GitLab group is literally named `collections` (it holds our asset
collections). Every repo inside it is now unusable as an APM dependency:

```
https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git
```

```
Invalid APM dependency
'https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git':
A subpath cannot be embedded in a git URL.
Got: `https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git`.
Use the `path:` key instead: `git: <repo-url>` + `path: <primitive>/<name>`
(or the shorthand `org/repo/<primitive>/<name>`).
```

Here `core` **is** the repository and `collections` **is** a real GitLab
subgroup. There is no embedded subpath.

## Reproduction

`apm.yml`:

```yaml
name: probe
version: 1.0.0
description: probe
author: probe
dependencies:
  apm:
    - https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git
marketplace:
  owner:
    name: probe
    url: https://example.com
  packages: []
```

`apm pack` -> exit 1.

## Observed behaviour matrix

| URL | Result | Correct? |
|---|---|---|
| `host/ai/collections/core.git` | REJECTED | NO - false positive |
| `host/ai/collections/core` | REJECTED | NO - false positive |
| `host/collections/core.git` (primitive at index 1) | accepted | yes |
| `host/org/repo/skills/my-skill` | REJECTED | yes - genuine |
| `host/ai/collection/core.git` (singular) | accepted | yes |

## Root cause

`src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py`, `_check_no_embedded_subpath`
(~L735):

```python
for idx, seg in enumerate(segments[:-1]):
    if idx >= 2 and seg in DependencyReference._APM_PRIMITIVE_DIRS:
        raise ValueError("A subpath cannot be embedded in a git URL. ...")
```

`_APM_PRIMITIVE_DIRS` (~L195) contains `collections`.

The `idx >= 2` scoping already acknowledges this exact false-positive class.
Its comment says it exists so as not to trip on "a subgroup literally named
after a primitive at index 1 (`group/skills/repo`)".

That reasoning is right, but the threshold assumes the repo prefix is exactly
`org/repo` - a GitHub assumption. **GitLab supports arbitrarily deep subgroup
nesting**, so a subgroup named after a primitive can legitimately appear at any
index, not just index 1. Any GitLab user with 2+ levels of nesting and a
subgroup named `collections`, `agents`, `prompts`, `instructions`, `contexts`,
or `memory` hits this.

Note `_GITLAB_VIRTUAL_ROOT_SEGMENTS` (L190, used L1106) also contains
`collections`, so this name is doubly special-cased on the GitLab path.

## Why there is no workaround

The guard runs in `_parse_dependency_string` **before** any form-specific
branching, so the object form is rejected identically:

```yaml
- git: https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git
```

Same error. The error text advises `git:` + `path:`, but there is no subpath to
move into `path:` - the URL is already just a repo URL. No spelling of the URL
avoids the guard. The only workaround is renaming the GitLab group, which for
an org-wide group means breaking every existing consumer.

## Suggested fix

The URL already carries an unambiguous signal that it is a complete repository
URL: the **`.git` suffix**. `_check_no_embedded_subpath` strips it and then
discards that information:

```python
if path_part.endswith(".git"):
    path_part = path_part[:-4]
```

A URL ending in `.git` terminates at the repository, so it cannot contain an
embedded subpath. Skipping the guard when the original URL ended in `.git`
would fix this class of false positive without weakening genuine detection -
users writing the malformed `org/repo/skills/name` shorthand do not append
`.git`. This mirrors the existing `_git` escape hatch already used for Azure
DevOps (~L723).

Failing that, an explicit opt-out (e.g. a manifest flag, or honouring the
absence of `path:` as intent) would unblock affected GitLab orgs.

## Environment

- apm-cli 0.26.0 (also reproduced on 0.28.0 in CI, `python:3.12` image)
- GitLab self-managed, group nesting depth 4

## Performance Scan - 2026-08-10

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [C] Unconditional Expensive Operation -- src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py:875,1206

- Current: `self.base_dir.resolve()` is called inside `_file_matches_pattern()` on every
  invocation, which is called once per file per directory per unique apply_to pattern
  in `_find_matching_directories()`. Since `__init__` already sets
  `self.base_dir = Path(base_dir).resolve()` (line 144), this is a redundant
  `os.path.realpath()` syscall. A secondary occurrence at line 1206 in
  `_get_relative_depth()` repeats the same waste.
- Proposed: O(0 extra syscalls) -- `self.base_dir` is already resolved; no re-resolve needed.
- Fix: Replace `self.base_dir.resolve()` with `self.base_dir` at lines 875 and 1206;
  the path is guaranteed resolved at construction time so the redundant call is a no-op
  that still pays the syscall overhead on every file match.

#### [C] Redundant Full-Tree Glob Scan -- src/apm_cli/deps/aggregator.py:17-21

- Current: `scan_workflows_for_dependencies()` issues two `glob.glob()` recursive
  tree walks: `**/.github/prompts/*.prompt.md` followed by `**/*.prompt.md`. The
  first pattern is a strict subset of the second (every path matched by the first
  is also matched by the second), so the first full-tree walk produces no unique
  results after the deduplication step at line 23. Two O(n) filesystem walks are
  performed where one suffices.
- Proposed: O(n) with a single `glob.glob("**/*.prompt.md", recursive=True)` pass.
- Fix: Remove the first (narrower) pattern from `prompt_patterns`; the broader
  `**/*.prompt.md` already covers `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md` paths. (Low priority:
  this is a developer-utility function, not the main install hot path.)

issues.title: [BUG] `apm compile --global` reports "no global instructions" with no discoverable authoring path
issues.body:
**Environment:** APM 0.28.0 (e041462), installed via the `microsoft/apm` Homebrew tap. macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64.

---


**Summary**

The CHANGELOG for 0.28.0 states:

> `apm compile -g / --global` compiles global (`apply_to`-less) instructions into user-scope root context files

I could not find any location where a user-scope global instruction is picked up. Every target reports `skipped (no global instructions)`.

**Repro**

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/fh2/.apm/.apm/instructions /tmp/fh2/.apm/instructions
printf 'Always prefer boring solutions.\n' > /tmp/fh2/.apm/.apm/instructions/probe.instructions.md
printf 'Always prefer boring solutions.\n' > /tmp/fh2/.apm/instructions/probe.instructions.md
HOME=/tmp/fh2 apm compile --global -v
```

```
claude: skipped (no global instructions)
...
[i] No user-scope root context files changed.
```

Also tried, all with the same result: both locations with an `applyTo: "**"` frontmatter block, and with a package installed globally that ships an `instructions` primitive (its rule deployed to `~/.claude/rules/` at install, but contributed nothing to compile).

**Ask**

Either this is broken, or the authoring location is undocumented. https://microsoft.github.io/apm/consumer/install-packages/ says targets needing a root context file "require explicit `apm compile --global`" but does not say where global instructions live. A line in the docs with the expected path would resolve it if this is user error.

**Minor:** `--global` is mutually exclusive with both `--target` and `--no-dedup`/`--force-instructions`, which is not obvious from the help text.

issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-08-12

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [E] Heavy Top-Level Import -- src/apm_cli/commands/update.py:62-68

- Current: O(startup) -- `from git.exc import GitCommandError` and `from ..deps.github_downloader import GitHubPackageDownloader` are loaded at module level; since cli.py eagerly imports all command modules, gitpython and the full download machinery load on every `apm` invocation regardless of which sub-command is run (e.g. `apm list`, `apm doctor`).
- Proposed: O(0) at startup -- import cost deferred to invocation time by moving these imports inside the `update` callback function body.
- Fix: Move `from git.exc import GitCommandError`, `from ..deps.github_downloader import GitHubPackageDownloader`, and the `revision_pins` imports inside the `update()` function body so they are only imported when `apm update` is actually invoked.

#### [B] Double Linear Scan on List -- src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py:1155-1156, 1322-1323, 1397-1398, 1503-1504

- Current: O(2n) per occurrence -- the pattern `if "_git" in parts: git_idx = parts.index("_git")` performs two sequential O(n) list scans (one membership check, one index lookup) where a single scan suffices. Appears four times across parse methods; called once per dependency string parsed at install/update time.
- Proposed: O(n) with a single scan -- use `try: git_idx = parts.index("_git") ... except ValueError: pass` or precompute the index once.
- Fix: Replace each `if "_git" in parts: idx = parts.index("_git")` pair with `try: idx = parts.index("_git"); parts = parts[:idx] + parts[idx+1:] except ValueError: pass` to eliminate the redundant membership scan.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (430 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-08-14
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-14
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (3aa0365)
**Commands Inspected**: 29 (23 from task spec + 6 discovered: `mcp list`, `runtime list`, `runtime status`, `runtime remove`, `config unset`, `deps why`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 1     |
| Low      | 3     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps update --target` has a stale, truncated target list

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The `--target` help text lists only 11 targets, while the non-deprecated sibling `apm update` lists 21. The following targets present in `apm update`, `apm install`, and `apm compile` are missing from `apm deps update`: `agents`, `agy`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-build`, `grok-cloud`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode`. The description of what `all` expands to is also outdated (still says the old set without the newer targets).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm deps update --help
  -t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                       copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                       gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-
                       skills, all. 'all' = co
                       pilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+wind
                       surf+kiro (excludes agent-skills and
                       antigravity)

  # apm update --help
  -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                       skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                       codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                       cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-cloud,
                       hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode,
                       vscode, windsurf.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: `apm deps update` is deprecated (`DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead`) and forwards to the same pipeline, so its `--target` help string should either be updated to match `apm update`'s full target list, or the help should redirect users to `apm update --help` for the authoritative flag reference.

---

### Low Severity

#### Trailing period inconsistency in top-level command list

- **Command**: `apm --help` (all commands)
- **Problem**: 16 commands end their one-line description with a period; 17 do not. This mixed punctuation style is inconsistent across the same list.
- **Evidence** (commands WITH a trailing period):
  `approve`, `audit`, `config`, `deny`, `doctor`, `find`, `install`, `lifecycle`, `lock`, `pack`, `prune`, `publish`, `self-update`, `targets`, `uninstall`, `unpack`
  
  Commands WITHOUT a trailing period (sample):
  `cache`, `compile`, `deps`, `experimental`, `init`, `list`, `marketplace`, `mcp`, `outdated`, `plugin`, `policy`, `preview`, `run`, `runtime`, `search`, `update`, `view`
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize all one-line descriptions to either consistently omit or include a trailing period. The majority currently omit it (17 vs 16), so removing the period from the 16 with periods would be the smallest diff. Note: descriptions that are truncated with `...` in the top-level list are not affected by this rule.

#### `-y, --yes` flag has three different descriptions across commands

- **Command**: `apm deps clean`, `apm update`, `apm runtime remove`
- **Problem**: Three commands use the same flag with three different descriptions:
  - `apm deps clean`: `Skip confirmation prompt`
  - `apm update`: `Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)`
  - `apm runtime remove`: `Confirm the action without prompting`
- **Evidence** (from `--help` of each command):
  ```
  apm deps clean:    -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt
  apm update:        -y, --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)
  apm runtime remove:-y, --yes  Confirm the action without prompting
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize to a single phrasing, e.g. `Skip the confirmation prompt`.

#### `apm deps clean` description slightly misleading

- **Command**: `apm deps clean`
- **Problem**: The command description is "Remove all APM dependencies" but the command only removes the `apm_modules/` directory. It does not remove `apm.yml` or `apm.lock.yaml`. A user reading this might expect all APM-related files to be removed.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm deps clean [OPTIONS]

    Remove all APM dependencies
  ```
  The docs (`deps.md`) correctly say "Remove the entire project `apm_modules/` directory. Does not touch `apm.yml` or `apm.lock.yaml`." -- the CLI help is less precise.
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the description to something like "Remove the installed `apm_modules/` directory" to match the precision of the docs.

---

### Clean Areas

- All 29 inspected commands and subcommands responded to `--help` without errors or tracebacks.
- Error handling is clean: invalid flags, missing required arguments, and missing subcommand arguments all produce structured `Usage:` + `Error:` messages with no stack traces.
- `--help` / `-h` works on every command and subcommand tested.
- `-v, --verbose` is consistently named (short and long form) and consistently described as "Show detailed output" or equivalent across all commands that support it.
- `--dry-run` is consistently named wherever applicable.
- `--global` / `-g` is consistently named and described across all commands that support it.
- All commands listed in `apm --help` exist and are functional.
- All doc pages under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` have a corresponding CLI command.
- The `mcp` subcommand group (`list`, `search`, `show`, `install`) matches its documentation page exactly.
- `config` subcommands (`get`, `list`, `set`, `unset`) match docs exactly.
- `runtime` subcommands (`setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove`) match docs exactly.

## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-17
**APM Version**: `Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.28.0 (8993dcc)`
**Commands Inspected**: 28 (23 from the task checklist + 5 additional: `apm mcp list`, `apm runtime remove`, `apm runtime status`, `apm deps why`, `apm config unset`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 2     |
| Low      | 2     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps why --help` examples are mangled by Click's word-wrap

- **Command**: `apm deps why --help`
- **Problem**: The help string in `src/apm_cli/commands/deps/why.py` defines three example lines using `\n` separators, but Click reflows them into a single paragraph because the `\b` escape is absent. The rendered output merges all three example lines and places `--json` at the start of a new terminal line disconnected from its command, making the examples look syntactically wrong.
- **Evidence** (actual terminal output):
  ```
    Examples:   apm deps why shared-utils   apm deps why acme-org/shared-utils
    --json   apm deps why shared-utils --global
  ```
  Expected (source intent from `src/apm_cli/commands/deps/why.py` lines 171-174):
  ```
  Examples:
    apm deps why shared-utils
    apm deps why acme-org/shared-utils --json
    apm deps why shared-utils --global
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Prepend `\b\n` before the `Examples:` label in `_HELP` so Click preserves the formatting:
  ```python
  _HELP = (
      "Explain why a package is installed by walking the lockfile back to "
      "one or more direct dependencies that pulled it in.\n\n"
      "\b\n"
      "Examples:\n"
      "  apm deps why shared-utils\n"
      "  apm deps why acme-org/shared-utils --json\n"
      "  apm deps why shared-utils --global"
  )
  ```

---

#### `apm install --update` is marked deprecated in help text but documentation does not reflect this

- **Command**: `apm install --update`
- **Problem**: The CLI help text explicitly marks `--update` as deprecated, but `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md` contains no deprecation notice for this flag. A user reading the docs would have no indication that `--update` is on a deprecation path.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI help output (`apm install --help`):
    ```
      --update   Update dependencies to latest Git references
                 (deprecated: prefer 'apm update' for an
                 interactive plan, or 'apm update --yes' for
                 CI). Unlike --refresh, --update restructures
                 the entire dependency graph.
    ```
  - `install.md` (line 32) describes `--update` with no deprecation notice:
    > `| --update | off | Re-resolve dependencies to the latest version or Git ref ... For interactive use with a confirmation prompt, use apm update instead. |`
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a `:::caution[Deprecated]` admonition to the `--update` row in `install.md` (mirroring the style used in `deps.md` for `apm deps update`), directing users to `apm update`.

---

### Low Severity

#### Deprecation notice style is inconsistent across commands

- **Commands**: `apm init --help` vs `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: Deprecated flags in `apm init --help` use lowercase `(deprecated)` prefix, while the entire `apm deps update` command description begins with all-caps `DEPRECATED:`. These two patterns are inconsistent.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm init --help`:
    ```
      --plugin      (deprecated) Use 'apm plugin init' instead. ...
      --marketplace (deprecated) Use 'apm marketplace init' instead. ...
    ```
  - `apm deps update --help`:
    ```
    DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset). Update APM
    dependencies to latest refs
    ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize on one style. The `(deprecated)` lowercase prefix (used by `apm init`) is the lower-noise convention. Consider updating `apm deps update` to use the same style, or adopt a project-wide convention and apply it uniformly.

---

#### `apm compile --all` help does not indicate `--target all` is deprecated

- **Command**: `apm compile --all`
- **Problem**: The `--all` flag's help text says it is "Equivalent to --target all" without noting that `--target all` emits a deprecation warning at runtime. A user who reads the help and decides to use `--target all` (as an equivalent form) will be surprised by the deprecation warning.

          Preferred form; --target all is deprecated and emits a warning.
  ```

---

### Clean Areas

- **All 28 `--help` invocations** responded without errors, panics, or stack traces.
- **Subcommand parity**: every subcommand listed in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` exists in the live CLI, and every subcommand shown in `--help` output is documented.
- **Flag naming is consistent**: `-v/--verbose`, `-g/--global`, `--dry-run`, `-y/--yes`, and `-t/--target` use identical names and short forms across every command that exposes them.
- **Error handling is clean**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (no arg), `apm config set` (no args), and `apm mcp search` (no arg) all return a concise usage + error message with no tracebacks.

issues.title: [BUG] Hook rewriting silently skips `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/path` — a quote between the variable and the separator defeats the matcher (residual gap from #1310)
issues.body:
## Summary

`_rewrite_command_for_target` only recognises a plugin-root reference when a path separator follows the closing brace **immediately**. A hook command that closes the quote first —

```json
"command": "python3 \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/hooks/probe.py"
```

— is not matched, so the script is never copied, the command is never rewritten, and **no warning is emitted**. `apm install` exits 0 and reports success. The raw `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` lands in `~/.claude/settings.json`, where Claude Code refuses it, producing the exact error from #1310 on every matching tool call:

> `PreToolUse:Bash hook error` — Failed to run: Hook command references `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` but the hook is not associated with a plugin. This variable is only available in hooks defined in a plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` file, not in settings.json files.

#1310 is closed and its fix works for `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/path`. This is the residual case that fix does not cover. `"${VAR}"/path` is valid, idiomatic shell — it quotes the part that can contain spaces — so plugin authors write it and get a silently dead hook.

## Root cause

`apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py:652` (v0.28.0):

```python
plugin_root_pattern = (
    r"\$\{(?:CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT|CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT|KIRO_PLUGIN_ROOT|PLUGIN_ROOT)\}"
    r"([\\/][^\s\"']+)"
)
for match in re.finditer(plugin_root_pattern, command):
    ...
    if source_file.exists() and source_file.is_file():
        ...copy + rewrite...
    else:
        _rich_warning(f"Hook script not found: {source_file}")
```

The group requires `[\\/]` right after `\}`. With a `"` there, `finditer` yields nothing.

Note that the "file not found" warning lives **inside the loop body**, so a command the pattern cannot match produces no diagnostic at all. The failure is completely silent — which is why this can sit undetected indefinitely.

## Reproduction

Self-contained, no external marketplace. Two plugins identical except for one quote position.

```
probe/
  .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
  plugins/probe-broken/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
  plugins/probe-broken/hooks/hooks.json
  plugins/probe-broken/hooks/probe.py
  plugins/probe-fixed/...          # same, different hooks.json
```

`plugins/probe-broken/hooks/hooks.json`:
```json
{"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[
  {"type":"command","command":"python3 \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/hooks/probe.py"}]}]}}
```

`plugins/probe-fixed/hooks/hooks.json` — identical but for the closing quote:
```json
{"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[
  {"type":"command","command":"python3 \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/probe.py\""}]}]}}
```

```console
$ git -C probe init -b main && git -C probe add -A && git -C probe commit -m probe
$ apm marketplace add ./probe --name probe
$ apm install probe-broken@probe probe-fixed@probe -g -t claude
[*] Installed 2 APM dependencies in 0.1s.        # exit 0, no warnings
```

**Actual** — `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/probe.py                 <- unrewritten, hook is dead
python3 "$HOME/.claude/hooks/probe-fixed/hooks/probe.py"       <- correct
```

Only `probe-fixed`'s script is copied under `~/.claude/hooks/`. `probe-broken` deploys nothing and says nothing.

**Expected** — either both rewritten, or at minimum a warning that a plugin-root reference was found and not resolved.

## Suggested fix, and a trap in the obvious version

Naively widening the group to accept an optional quote (`\}["']?([\\/]...)`) produces a **broken command**: `full_var` then spans `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/probe.py`, and substituting the resolved path leaves the *opening* quote dangling —

```
python3 "/abs/path/hooks/probe.py      # unbalanced
```

A minimal safe fix is to normalise the quote pair before the existing matcher runs — rewrite `"${VAR}"/rest` to `"${VAR}/rest"` — which turns the unsupported spelling into the spelling that is already handled and already tested. Same for `'`.

Independently, moving the "not found" warning so that *any* unresolved plugin-root reference is reported would have surfaced this at install time rather than at every subsequent tool call.

## Environment

- apm 0.28.0 (78e05bb56f), Homebrew, Python 3.14
- macOS (arm64)
- user scope (`-g`), target `claude`

Related: #1310 (same symptom, fixed for the unquoted spelling), #1894 (per-package hook opt-out — would provide the missing workaround).

issues.title: [BUG] apm lock export --timestamp accepts invalid values without error
issues.body:
### Bug Summary

The `--timestamp` option in `apm lock export` lacks validation for ISO 8601 formatting. Consequently, arbitrary or malformed string values are accepted without error and embedded directly into the generated CycloneDX/SPDX Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) metadata. This causes silent generation of non-compliant SBOM artifacts that fail downstream schema verification.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Execute `apm lock export` with an invalid timestamp string:
   ```bash
   apm lock export --timestamp "not-a-date"
   ```
2. Observe that the command executes successfully (exit code 0) without any validation warnings or errors.

Other malformed inputs that bypass validation:
```bash
apm lock export --timestamp "   "
apm lock export --timestamp "99999-99-99"
apm lock export --timestamp "2024-13-45T99:99:99Z"
apm lock export --timestamp "hello world"
```

### Expected Behavior

The CLI should validate the timestamp against the ISO 8601 specification before generating the export artifact and fail gracefully on invalid input:

```
Error: Invalid value for '--timestamp': 'not-a-date' is not a valid ISO 8601 datetime (e.g. 2024-06-01T00:00:00+00:00).
```

### Environment

 - OS: macOS
 - Python Version: 3.12.0
 - APM Version: 0.28.0

### Command Output / Evidence

Output excerpt from `apm lock export --timestamp "not-a-date"`:

```json
"metadata": {
  "timestamp": "not-a-date"
}
```

The command terminates with exit status 0 despite generating an invalid ISO 8601 timestamp in the specification metadata.

### Technical Details & Root Cause

The CLI documentation explicitly defines the expected format:
> *"Pin the SBOM timestamp (ISO 8601, e.g. 2024-06-01T00:00:00+00:00) for reproducible output."*

However, in `src/apm_cli/commands/lock.py`, the helper `_resolve_export_timestamp` returns user input verbatim without checking specification compliance:

```python
def _resolve_export_timestamp(explicit: str | None, ...) -> str:
    if explicit:
        return explicit  # Bypasses ISO 8601 validation
```

Validating the string via `datetime.fromisoformat()` prior to serialization will prevent silent output corruption.

issues.title: [BUG] UTF-8 BOM on an instruction file silently drops its frontmatter: applyTo scope lost, metadata leaked into compiled output, exit 0
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

A UTF-8 BOM on an instruction file silently drops its frontmatter. `apm compile` exits 0, the declared `applyTo` scope is lost so the rule is applied globally, and the raw frontmatter block is emitted verbatim into the compiled context file.

`load_frontmatter` reads with `encoding="utf-8"` (`src/apm_cli/utils/yaml_io.py:492`), not `utf-8-sig`, so the BOM survives as a literal `﻿` before the line-1 `---` and the fence no longer matches.

The BOM then propagates into the generated `CLAUDE.md`, where APM's own audit flags it: `CLAUDE.md contains 1 hidden character(s)`.

This is a Windows-shaped trigger. PowerShell 5.1's `Out-File -Encoding utf8` and `>` both write a BOM, as does Notepad, so a package authored on Windows can carry one without the author ever seeing it.

**To Reproduce**

Two instruction files, identical except for the BOM:

```python
fm = '---\ndescription: Scoped rule\napplyTo: "**/*.py"\n---\n# Style\nUse type hints.\n'
Path('.apm/instructions/nobom.instructions.md').write_bytes(fm.encode('utf-8'))
Path('.apm/instructions/withbom.instructions.md').write_bytes(fm.encode('utf-8-sig'))
```

```console
$ apm compile --target claude
[!]   .apm/instructions/withbom.instructions.md: No 'applyTo' pattern specified
-- instruction will apply globally
[!]   CLAUDE.md contains 1 hidden character(s) -- run 'apm audit --file ...' to inspect
$ echo $?
0
```

Generated `CLAUDE.md` puts the BOM'd file under `### Global Instructions` with its metadata as body text:

```
### Global Instructions

﻿---
description: Scoped rule
applyTo: "**/*.py"
---
# Style
```

while the identical no-BOM file lands correctly under `### Files matching **/*.py`.

**Expected behavior**

Decode with `utf-8-sig` so a leading BOM is consumed, or fail loudly rather than silently downgrading a scoped rule to global.

**Environment**

- OS: Windows 11 Home 26200
- Python: 3.13.13
- APM: 0.28.0, verified on `main` at `88cf78a`

**Additional context**

Not a regression from #2666, which touches this function: I ran the same case on `main` (`88cf78a`) and on that PR's head (`d27ed4e`) and both lose the frontmatter identically. #372 handled a BOM in `strip_dangerous` only; this is the loader path.

Related failure profile to #2663 and #2624: exit 0 with a quietly wrong result.

I used an AI assistant to prepare this report. I ran the reproduction, the exit code, and the two-ref comparison myself on the machine described above.

issues.title: [BUG] Codex adapter rejects every non-https remote MCP URL, so loopback servers configure for all targets except Codex
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm mcp install --transport http --url http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` configures the server for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini and VS Code, but silently skips Codex CLI:

```
[!] Skipping MCP server 'demo' for Codex CLI: remote URL must use https:// (got http).
```

The check is in `apm_cli/adapters/client/codex.py` (0.28.0) and has no loopback exemption:

```python
scheme = urlparse(remote_url).scheme.lower()
if scheme != "https":
    _rich_warning(
        f"Skipping MCP server '{server_name}' for Codex CLI: remote URL "
        f"must use https:// (got {scheme or 'no scheme'}).",
        symbol="warning",
    )
    return None
```

`adapters/client/claude.py` has no URL scheme check at all, so one manifest produces different results per target.

This blocks a common shape: a local MCP bridge listening on 127.0.0.1 — for example anything fronting a stdio server over streamable HTTP. TLS on a loopback socket adds no confidentiality, and satisfying the check would mean provisioning a certificate and adding it to a trust store purely to pass a string comparison.

Notably, **Codex itself accepts a plain-http loopback URL.** A plugin-supplied server at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` appears in `codex mcp list` as `enabled` with `Auth = Bearer token`. The restriction appears to be APM's rather than Codex's.

**To Reproduce**

1. `apm init` in an empty directory
2. ```
   apm mcp install demo --transport http \
     --url http://127.0.0.1:4520/mcp \
     --header 'Authorization=Bearer ${MY_TOKEN}' \
     -t claude,codex,cursor,gemini,vscode
   ```
3. `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.gemini/settings.json` and `.vscode/mcp.json` all contain `demo`. `.codex/config.toml` does not.

Substituting an `https://` URL configures all five, which isolates the scheme as the only difference.

**Expected behavior**

Either exempt loopback hosts (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`) from the https requirement, or offer an opt-in flag. A loopback http endpoint is a normal deployment shape and is accepted by Codex itself.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- APM Version: 0.28.0 (533246d16f)

**Additional context**

Secondary observation, possibly deserving its own issue: in the run above `apm mcp install` **exits 0** while printing `x demo installation failed` and `[x] Failed to install demo`. Tooling that checks the return code reads the Codex refusal as success. The user-scope deploy verb (`apm install -g`) does return 1 in the equivalent case, so the two paths disagree.

issues.title: [BUG] apm pack --check-clean overwrites marketplace.json before checking drift
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm pack --check-clean` performs a normal marketplace build before running the clean check. In non-dry-run mode, the build overwrites the checked-in `marketplace.json`. The subsequent drift check then compares the regenerated file with itself and reports a clean result.

This makes `--check-clean` ineffective as a release gate when `--dry-run` is omitted.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Use a project with this marketplace configuration:

   ```yaml
   marketplace:
     output: .github/plugin/marketplace.json
     outputs:
       claude: {}
   ```

2. Ensure `.github/plugin/marketplace.json` matches `apm.yml`.
3. Change `marketplace.version` in `apm.yml` from `1.0.1` to `1.0.2`.
4. Run the command without `--dry-run`:

   ```bash
   apm pack --check-clean
   ```

5. Observe that the command exits with code `0` and rewrites `.github/plugin/marketplace.json`.
6. Confirm the mutation:

   ```bash
   git diff -- .github/plugin/marketplace.json
   ```

7. From the same pre-change state, run:

   ```bash
   apm pack --check-clean --dry-run
   ```

   This correctly reports drift and exits with code `4` without modifying the file.

**Expected behavior**

`--check-clean` should be read-only. It should compare the generated output with the existing file without overwriting the file being validated.

When drift exists, the command should leave the existing generated file unchanged, report the drift, and exit with code `4`.

Alternatively, APM should reject `--check-clean` when it is used without `--dry-run`, rather than silently mutating the generated file.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Windows
- Python Version: 3.9.16
- APM Version: 0.29.0

**Logs**

```text
Command:
apm pack --check-clean

Observed output:
[*] Built marketplace.json [claude] (1 package(s)) -> <project-root>\\.github\\plugin\\marketplace.json
[*] Marketplace working tree clean [outputs=claude]

Exit code:
0
```

With `--dry-run`, the same source/output mismatch reports marketplace drift and exits with code `4`.

**Additional context**

The current CI workaround is:

```bash
apm pack --check-clean --dry-run
```

The drift check itself does not write files. The problem is the command order: the normal `BuildOrchestrator` runs first with `dry_run=False`, and `check_marketplace_drift` runs afterward using a separate dry-run builder. The normal build has already updated the file before the comparison begins.

A regression test should verify that `apm pack --check-clean` never mutates an existing generated marketplace file and returns exit code `4` when the source manifest and generated output differ.

issues.title: [BUG] Legacy ledger synthesis labels .agents/ paths with target 'agents', which resolves to copilot (.github/)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`DeploymentLedgerCodec._legacy_locator()` attributes a deployed path to a target by matching a path prefix against `_LEGACY_TARGET_PREFIXES` (`apm_cli/core/deployment_ledger.py:29-39`). Every entry in that map resolves back to a real target profile **except `.agents/`**, which maps to the string `"agents"`.

`"agents"` is not a key in `KNOWN_TARGETS`, and `normalize_target_name("agents")` returns **`copilot`**, whose `root_dir` is **`.github`** — not `.agents`. APM's own deprecation warning states this explicitly:

> `'--target agents' is deprecated -- it maps to 'copilot' (.github/), not '.agents/'.`

So when the deployment ledger is synthesized from the legacy `deployed_files` views (`from_lockfile`, `deployment_ledger.py:180-192`, taken whenever a lockfile carries no canonical `deployments:` block), every `.agents/...` row is written with a target that names a **different target owning a different root**.

`.agents/` is additionally a *shared* root — `codex`, `agent-skills`, `hermes`, `openclaw` and `antigravity` all deploy there — so a single prefix cannot identify its owner. The other prefixes in the map (`.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.github/`, `.cursor/`, …) are each owned by exactly one target and round-trip correctly.

**To Reproduce**

Pure-function repro, no APM command run and no `~/.apm` state touched:

```python
import warnings; warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
from apm_cli.core.deployment_ledger import DeploymentLedgerCodec
from apm_cli.core.target_catalog import normalize_target_name
from apm_cli.integration.targets import KNOWN_TARGETS

for p in [".agents/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md",   # subject
          ".claude/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md",   # control
          ".codex/agents/my-agent.toml",        # control
          ".github/agents/my-agent.agent.md"]:  # control
    t = DeploymentLedgerCodec._legacy_locator(p).target
    norm = normalize_target_name(t)
    root = getattr(KNOWN_TARGETS.get(norm), "root_dir", "—")
    print(f"{p:38} target={t:8} normalizes={norm:8} in KNOWN_TARGETS={t in KNOWN_TARGETS!s:5} root={root}")
```

Output, identical on 0.28.0 and 0.29.0:

```
.agents/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md       target=agents   normalizes=copilot  in KNOWN_TARGETS=False root=.github   <-- mismatch
.claude/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md       target=claude   normalizes=claude   in KNOWN_TARGETS=True  root=.claude   ok
.codex/agents/my-agent.toml            target=codex    normalizes=codex    in KNOWN_TARGETS=True  root=.codex    ok
.github/agents/my-agent.agent.md       target=copilot  normalizes=copilot  in KNOWN_TARGETS=True  root=.github   ok
```

Three controls round-trip; only the subject does not, so the check discriminates.

**Expected behavior**

A synthesized legacy row should carry a target that actually owns the path, or the sentinel the function already has for "unattributable" (`"legacy"`, the `next(..., "legacy")` default two lines below). It should not name a target whose deploy root does not contain the path.

Because `.agents/` is shared by several targets, prefix matching cannot identify its owner from the path alone. Options that would both be sound: fall back to `"legacy"` for `.agents/`, or resolve the owner from the declared/active target set rather than the prefix.

**Environment**
- OS: macOS 26.6.2
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- APM Version: 0.28.0 and 0.29.0 (both reproduce; `_LEGACY_TARGET_PREFIXES` is byte-identical between them)

**Additional context**

Observed after upgrading 0.28.0 → 0.29.0 with a pre-existing lockfile, where a `user`-scope (`-g`) install produced a ledger with 233 rows labelled `target: agents` for `.agents/skills/...` paths, alongside correctly-labelled `claude` and `codex` rows for the same install. Re-running with the lockfile moved aside produced a ledger with no `agents` rows at all and correct per-target attribution.

I have not traced whether the mislabelled rows are what drove the subsequent reconciliation outcome, so I am reporting only the attribution defect above, which is self-contained and independently reproducible.

issues.title: [BUG] apm install of a claude-plugin bundle doesn't retarget commands/ to prompts/ for --target copilot
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`apm pack --format claude-plugin` converts a `prompts/` primitive (from `.apm/prompts/*.prompt.md`) into Claude-native `commands/*.md` inside the bundle. When that packed bundle is later installed with `apm install <bundle> --target copilot`, the installer deploys `commands/*.md` verbatim to `.github/commands/*.md` instead of retargeting it to Copilot's native convention (`.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`).

Installing the same primitives from the **source** APM project (i.e. a path/git URL containing `.apm/` + `apm.yml`, not a packed bundle) with the same `--target copilot` flag retargets correctly, producing `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`. So the retargeting logic exists in the source-install/compile path but is not applied when installing a pre-packed `claude-plugin` bundle.

Agents and instructions are unaffected because their Claude-native folder names (`agents/`, `instructions/`) happen to match Copilot's convention. `commands/` vs `prompts/` is the one primitive type where the naming diverges, so it's the one that breaks.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create/use an APM project with a prompt primitive, e.g. `.apm/prompts/generate-api-docs.prompt.md`, and `targets: [copilot]` in `apm.yml`.
2. Pack it: `apm pack --format claude-plugin -o ./dist`
   - Inspect the bundle: the prompt is now at `dist/<pkg>-<version>/commands/generate-api-docs.md`.
3. In a fresh consumer project (`apm init . --target copilot -y`), install the packed bundle:
   `apm install ../path/to/dist/<pkg>-<version>/ --target copilot -v`
4. Inspect the consumer's `.github/`:
   - Actual: `.github/commands/generate-api-docs.md`
   - Expected: `.github/prompts/generate-api-docs.prompt.md`

For comparison, installing the **source** project instead of the packed bundle works correctly:
`apm install ../path/to/source-project --target copilot -v`
→ logs `1 prompts integrated -> .github/prompts/` and produces `.github/prompts/generate-api-docs.prompt.md`.

**Expected behavior**
`apm install` of a packed `claude-plugin` bundle should retarget primitive directories/extensions per `--target`/`apm.yml targets:`, the same way installing from source does — i.e. `commands/*.md` → `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md` when the target is `copilot`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- APM CLI version: 0.29.0
- OS: Windows 11
- Reproduced with a local-path bundle install (no registry involved)

**Additional context**
There is no `apm pack` flag to keep the prompt primitive as `prompts/` (or otherwise avoid the rename), and neither alternative format is a viable substitute:
- `--format claude-plugin` (the only format that currently packs agents/instructions/prompts at all) unconditionally renames `prompts/` to `commands/`, with no option to override. The generated `plugin.json` is bare metadata (name/version/author/license) — it doesn't record primitive types anywhere an install step could use to translate the folder back, so the folder name is the only signal, and by pack time it's already Claude-flavored.
- `--format agent-plugin` is not a substitute either: it's a portable spec limited to `skills/`, `plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, so it drops prompts (and agents/instructions) entirely rather than mis-naming them.
- `--format apm` (legacy APM bundle layout) produced an **empty** bundle for this same project — `apm pack --format apm -o ./dist-apm --force` logged "No deployed files found -- empty bundle created" even after `--force`. So today it isn't a working alternative regardless of the naming question. Happy to file that as a separate issue if useful — mentioning here since it rules out one path around the main bug.

Net effect: as of 0.29.0, there is currently no supported way to pack a prompt primitive into a distributable bundle and have it install correctly for a Copilot-targeted consumer.

issues.title: [BUG] Lockfile generation fails on multiple OneDrive mounts even when copilot-cowork is disabled
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Running `apm install` (e.g. `apm install github/awesome-copilot/skills/refactor --global --verbose`) on APM v0.29.0 fails during lockfile generation with:
`Could not generate apm.lock.yaml: Multiple OneDrive mounts detected:`

This occurs on macOS systems with multiple OneDrive mounts under `~/Library/CloudStorage/`, even when:
1. `copilot-cowork` is not specified as an active target.
2. The `copilot-cowork` experimental feature is explicitly **disabled** (verified with `apm experimental list`).
3. The exact same command succeeded on APM v0.28.0.

This appears to be a regression / wider manifestation of #2395.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. On a macOS machine with multiple OneDrive mounts under `~/Library/CloudStorage/` (and `copilot-cowork` disabled in `apm experimental list`):
2. Run:
   ```bash
   apm install github/awesome-copilot/skills/refactor --global --verbose
   ```
3. See error during the lockfile phase: `Could not generate apm.lock.yaml: Multiple OneDrive mounts detected:`

**Expected behavior**

APM should not trigger OneDrive discovery or Cowork resolution when `copilot-cowork` is not an active target and its experimental flag is disabled. Package installation and lockfile generation should succeed.

**Root Cause Analysis**

In `src/apm_cli/install/phases/lockfile.py`, `_attach_deployed_files()` calls `declared_target_profiles()` from `apm_cli.install.phases.targets`, which delegates to `apm_cli.install.manifest_reconcile.declared_target_profiles()`.

In `src/apm_cli/install/manifest_reconcile.py`:
```python
for name, profile in KNOWN_TARGETS.items():
    if name in CANONICAL_TARGETS:
        continue
    scoped = profile.for_scope(user_scope=user_scope)
    profiles.append(scoped if scoped is not None else profile)
```

`copilot-cowork` is in `KNOWN_TARGETS` as a non-canonical target. Calling `for_scope(user_scope=True)` immediately invokes its `user_root_resolver` (`resolve_copilot_cowork_skills_dir`), which scans `~/Library/CloudStorage/` and raises `CoworkResolutionError` when multiple mounts are found. Because this is unhandled and not gated on `copilot-cowork` being enabled/targeted, it aborts `LockfileBuilder.execute()`.

**Environment:**
- OS: macOS
- Python Version: `3.14.7`
- APM Version: `Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.29.0 (5ac6733)`

**Logs**

*(Sanitized)*

```text
[*] Validating 1 package...
[>] Installing 1 new package...
Parsed apm.yml: 3 APM deps, 0 MCP deps
Using apm.lock.yaml (3 locked dependencies)
Active global targets: copilot (~/.copilot/), claude (~/.claude/), codex (~/.codex/)
Lockfile: /Users/<username>/.apm/apm.lock.yaml
Phase: targets -> 0.002s
Copilot native registration: available (copilot targeted)
Phase: download -> 0.002s
Phase: integrate -> 0.060s
[x] Could not generate apm.lock.yaml: Multiple OneDrive mounts detected:
  - /Users/<username>/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-<organization>
  - /Users/<username>/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-SharedLibraries-<shared-dir>
Set APM_COPILOT_COWORK_SKILLS_DIR to the desired skills directory, e.g.:

issues.title: [BUG] MCP server args and lock content hash recorded from the .apm-resolution-staging replacement path; the path vanishes after install
issues.body:
## Summary

A transitive package that goes through the resolution-staging "replacement" path can end up with its MCP server `args` recorded as the *staging* location, in `apm.lock.yaml`, `~/.claude.json` and `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  context-mode:
    command: node
    args:
    - /Users/<me>/.apm/apm_modules/.apm-resolution-staging/a1e585cd970240fc9c2486c04372d68a/replacements/c0524b8a…/start.mjs
```

The staging root is removed when the transaction completes, so every later MCP startup fails (`handshaking with MCP server failed: connection closed`), while `apm install -g` keeps reporting success because the lock entry is adopted as-is.

Seen with `mksglu/context-mode` pulled in transitively by a local `path:` package, user scope, `apm install -g --trust-transitive-mcp`, apm 0.29.0 at `656f3d6`.

## Where it comes from

`src/apm_cli/install/resolution_staging.py`: `prepare_replacement()` hands out an isolated path under `.apm-resolution-staging/<session>/replacements/…`, and the package is only moved to its live `apm_modules/<owner>/<repo>` location in `publish_replacement()`. If MCP integration (self-defined MCP servers in the package's `apm.yml`, `--trust-transitive-mcp` path) resolves script paths relative to the package directory *before* `publish_replacement()` runs, the recorded path is the staging one.

Secondary effect: the lock's content hash for that dependency was computed on the replacement tree. After the staging dir is gone and the operator repairs the `args` by hand, every install fails with `Content hash mismatch for mksglu/context-mode … Use 'apm install --update'`, and `--update` restructures the whole graph, which moved unrelated unpinned dependencies in my case.

## Expected

- MCP server `args` (and any deployment path) are always derived from the published live path, never from a staging path. Simplest: compute them after `publish_replacement()`, or map staging → live before writing the lock and the client configs.
- A staged replacement's content hash is written only for the published tree.
- Defensive check: refuse to write a lock or client config that contains `.apm-resolution-staging`.

## Workaround used

Replace the staging path with `~/.apm/apm_modules/mksglu/context-mode/start.mjs` in the three files, then `apm install -g --update` to accept the recomputed hash (and re-pin anything it moved).

## Environment

- apm 0.29.0 from commit `656f3d6e6dbade369b6fc8727a4eb7b164409b6d`
- macOS 15 arm64, targets `claude` + `codex`, user scope

issues.title: [BUG] Negative prune days delete the Git checkout cache
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm cache prune` accepts negative values for `--days`. A negative value creates a future cutoff time, causing all existing Git checkout cache entries to be pruned.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Populate the Git checkout cache.
2. Run `apm cache prune --days -1`.
3. Observe that all cached checkouts are removed and the command exits successfully.

**Expected behavior**

The command should reject negative values with a validation error and leave the cache unchanged.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Windows
- Python Version: 3.14
- APM Version: 0.29.1
- VSCode Version: Not relevant
