issues.title: [FEATURE] Support atomic exact dependency reconciliation for global installs
issues.body:
## Use case

A user is writing a script on top of APM.

The script must enforce a complete desired state for one package, such as an APM package stored in a Git repository.

The script supplies:

- The existing dependency’s canonical identity
- The desired package source and ref
- The complete desired skill subset
- The complete desired dependency-target subset
- Any missing targets that must become globally active

The script should not need to read and merge the package’s existing selection before invoking APM.

APM can read the existing declaration to locate it and produce a plan. However, existing skills and dependency targets must not affect the requested replacement values.

Without this capability, the script must parse and rewrite `~/.apm/apm.yml`. It must also reproduce APM’s identity, validation, locking, deployment, and recovery behavior.

A supported APM operation would let the script declare the desired package state while APM retains ownership of its manifest and installation transaction.

## Reproduction

I reproduced this behavior with APM 0.29.0 and an isolated home directory.

The local package contains these skills:

```text
accessibility-guide
legacy-reviewer
python-style-guide
```

The package has no producer target restriction.

A local package avoids network access while exercising the same skill-subset and dependency-target mutation path. I normalized only the temporary directory name below.

## State A

The global consumer manifest at `~/.apm/apm.yml` starts with:

```yaml
name: isolated-global-consumer
version: 1.0.0

targets:
  - agent-skills
  - claude
  - kiro

dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle
      skills:
        - legacy-reviewer
        - python-style-guide
      targets:
        - claude
        - kiro
```

## Desired state B

The user wants this exact global consumer state:

```yaml
name: isolated-global-consumer
version: 1.0.0

targets:
  - agent-skills
  - claude
  - kiro
  - cursor

dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle
      skills:
        - accessibility-guide
        - python-style-guide
      targets:
        - cursor
        - kiro
```

This transition must:

- Add `accessibility-guide`.
- Remove `legacy-reviewer`.
- Add `cursor` to the dependency targets.
- Remove `claude` from the dependency targets.
- Retain `kiro` in the dependency targets.
- Add `cursor` to the top-level active targets.
- Preserve all existing top-level targets, including `claude`.

The effective targets for this dependency become:

```text
[agent-skills, claude, kiro, cursor]
INTERSECT
[cursor, kiro]
=
[cursor, kiro]
```

Removing `claude` from the dependency does not remove it from the global active-target list.

## Closest existing command

The closest existing command is:

```console
apm install --global \
  /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle \
  --skill accessibility-guide \
  --skill python-style-guide \
  --target cursor,kiro
```

The relevant actual output was:

```text
[*] Validating 1 package...
[+] /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle (updated ref in apm.yml)
[*] Updated apm.yml dependency entries
[>] Installing 1 new package...
  [+] /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle (local)
  |-- 3 skill(s) integrated -> .agents/skills/, .kiro/skills/
[*] Installed 1 APM dependency
```

The resulting global manifest was:

```yaml
name: isolated-global-consumer
version: 1.0.0

targets:
  - agent-skills
  - claude
  - kiro

dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle
      skills:
        - accessibility-guide
        - legacy-reviewer
        - python-style-guide
```

This is not state B:

- `--skill` unions the requested skills with the existing subset.
- `legacy-reviewer` remains selected.
- The positional rewrite removes the dependency-level target restriction.
- `--target cursor,kiro` applies only to this invocation.
- `cursor` is not added to the top-level active targets.
- The exact dependency-target restriction is not persisted.

In this reproduced package, no producer restriction, policy rule, or collision blocked deployment.

APM therefore deployed the unioned three skills to the invocation’s `cursor` and `kiro` targets.

A later bare global install cannot reproduce the requested selection from the resulting manifest.

The current additive `--skill` behavior is useful and should remain the default.

## Current workaround

The script can edit `~/.apm/apm.yml` directly and then run:

```console
apm install --global
```

This works because the manifest contains the desired state before APM starts.

However, the script must implement behavior that belongs to APM:

- Dependency identity matching
- Exact dependency replacement
- Top-level target activation
- YAML round-trip preservation
- Atomic file replacement
- Failure recovery

The manifest mutation and installation are also separate operations.

## Requested capability

Please provide one APM operation that accepts the complete desired state for one global direct Git dependency.

The existing dependency selector must be separate from the desired Git source. This permits APM to locate the old declaration before it writes the replacement.

The final CLI design is open. One illustrative shape is:

```console
apm install --global example-org/skill-bundle#v1.2.3 \
  --replace-dependency example-org/skill-bundle \
  --exact-skills accessibility-guide,python-style-guide \
  --exact-package-targets cursor,kiro \
  --ensure-package-targets-active
```

In this example:

- `--replace-dependency` identifies the existing canonical dependency.
- The positional package reference supplies the desired Git source and ref.
- `--exact-skills` supplies the complete skill subset.
- `--exact-package-targets` supplies the complete dependency-target restriction.
- `--ensure-package-targets-active` adds missing dependency targets to the top-level list.

The option names are illustrative. The required behavior is more important than the final syntax.

Existing `--skill` behavior must remain additive when exact replacement is not requested.

## Exact replacement behavior

For this use case, the operation applies to direct Git dependencies under `dependencies.apm`.

The desired managed declaration consists of:

- Git source
- Ref
- Skill subset
- Dependency-target subset

The operation must not union existing skills or dependency targets into those requested values.

It should behave as an exact upsert:

- If the selector exists in neither dependency section, add the desired declaration under `dependencies.apm`.
- If exactly one declaration matches under `dependencies.apm`, replace it with the complete desired declaration.
- If duplicate declarations with the same selected identity exist under `dependencies.apm`, consolidate them into one normalized desired declaration.
- If the selector is ambiguous, fail before mutation.
- If the selected identity appears under `devDependencies.apm`, fail instead of adding or changing a production declaration.
- If the declaration already matches, retain it and perform normal installation reconciliation.

The same desired-state command should handle every valid starting state.

## Global target behavior

The operation must ensure that every desired dependency target is active at the top level.

It must add missing targets without removing or replacing existing top-level targets.

For the state A to state B transition, it adds only `cursor`:

```yaml
targets:
  - agent-skills
  - claude
  - kiro
  - cursor
```

Adding `cursor` changes the global active-target universe. An unrelated dependency without its own target restriction can become eligible for Cursor deployment during a later global install.

This effect is intentional in state B and must appear in the operation’s plan.

The operation must preserve unrelated dependency declarations. It must not silently rewrite them.

## Transaction and validation behavior

The operation should use the normal APM policy, source-validation, integrity, lockfile, target-filtering, deployment, and cleanup paths.

It should apply one durable APM transaction containing:

1. The additive top-level active-target change.
2. The exact selected dependency declaration.
3. The normal lockfile update.
4. The normal installation reconciliation for the selected dependency.

Validation, resolution, or activation failure must retain the previous manifest and lockfile state.

Deployment and cleanup should retain APM’s existing ownership, hash, and recovery protections.

Package resolution and deployment should remain scoped to the selected dependency and its required transitive graph.

`--dry-run` should show:

- The existing dependency selector
- The complete replacement declaration
- The top-level targets that will be added
- The selected package’s deployment changes
- Global eligibility changes caused by activating a target

## Idempotence and determinism

The user should not have to reconstruct the dependency’s current state before invoking the command.

Different valid starting declarations should converge to the same desired declaration.

Repeating the command after a successful and consistent installation should produce no additional managed-state change.

This guarantee covers:

- `~/.apm/apm.yml`
- `~/.apm/apm.lock.yaml`
- Managed files for the selected package

Mutable Git refs can resolve differently over time. Reproducible source resolution still requires an immutable ref, lockfile, or frozen workflow.

## OpenAPM alignment

[OpenAPM v0.1](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/specs/openapm-v01/) already defines:

- Top-level active targets
- Consumer-authorized dependency-target subsets
- Producer target restrictions
- Per-dependency skill subsets

This request does not require a new manifest field.

It requests one APM-owned operation across two existing consumer-manifest surfaces:

1. Exact replacement of one direct dependency declaration.
2. Additive activation of missing top-level targets.

APM already owns dependency identity, subset validation, target intersection, lock state, deployment, cleanup, and recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One global APM operation transforms state A into state B.
2. Existing dependency skills and targets do not affect the exact replacement.
3. The desired Git source, ref, skills, and dependency targets form the replacement declaration.
4. `cursor` is added to both the dependency restriction and top-level targets.
5. `claude` is removed only from the dependency restriction.
6. Every existing top-level target remains present.
7. Unrelated dependency declarations and manifest fields remain unchanged.
8. An absent direct dependency is added with the exact requested state.
9. Same-identity duplicates under `dependencies.apm` become one desired declaration.
10. A conflicting development dependency or ambiguous selector fails before mutation.
11. An already-correct declaration produces no additional managed-state change.
12. Validation, resolution, or activation failure retains the prior manifest and lockfile state.
13. Existing deployment ownership and cleanup protections remain active.
14. Existing additive `--skill` behavior remains unchanged.
15. `--dry-run` reports dependency, deployment, and global-target effects.

issues.title: [BUG] Installer declares glibc 2.35 floor but prebuilt Linux binary requires 2.38 (fails at dynamic-link time on glibc 2.36/2.37)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The Unix installer (`https://aka.ms/apm-unix`) gates on `REQUIRED_GLIBC="2.35"`, but the prebuilt Linux binary's bundled `libpython3.12.so.1.0` requires **`GLIBC_2.38`**. Systems with glibc **2.36 or 2.37 pass the installer's version check and then fail at dynamic-link time**, which is a much more confusing failure than an upfront rejection.

Affects `linux-x86_64` and `linux-arm64`, and is still present in **v0.30.0** (latest) and the currently-served installer.

**Evidence**

The binary's own symbol versions, from the v0.29.0 release asset:

```console
$ readelf -V apm-linux-x86_64/_internal/libpython3.12.so.1.0 | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | sort -uV | tail -3
GLIBC_2.34
GLIBC_2.35
GLIBC_2.38
```

The four symbols responsible:

```console
$ readelf -sW .../libpython3.12.so.1.0 | grep GLIBC_2.38 | awk '{print $8}' | sort -u
__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38
__isoc23_strtoul@GLIBC_2.38
__isoc23_wcstol@GLIBC_2.38
fmod@GLIBC_2.38
```

The `__isoc23_*` symbols are the C23 variants glibc introduced in **2.38**; GCC emits them automatically when building against a 2.38+ system. This suggests the release is **built on a host with glibc ≥ 2.38**, silently raising the runtime floor above the declared 2.35 — rather than being a deliberate floor choice.

**To Reproduce**

As root in Docker on `linux/amd64`:

```console
$ docker run --rm node:22-bookworm sh -c \
    'curl -fsSL https://aka.ms/apm-unix | sh -s -- "@v0.29.0" --prefix /usr/local'
[PYI-68:ERROR] Failed to load Python shared library '.../libpython3.12.so.1.0':
  /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
[!] glibc version incompatibility detected
Your system has glibc 2.36 but the binary requires glibc 2.35+
```

Note the final line reports 2.36 ≥ 2.35 while simultaneously failing.

| Image | glibc | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `node:22-bullseye` (Debian 11) | 2.31 | rejected by the version check (correct) |
| `node:22-bookworm` (Debian 12) | 2.36 | **passes the check, then fails linking** |
| `node:22-trixie` (Debian 13) | 2.41 | works |

**Three places state 2.35**

A fix that changes only the constant leaves two user-facing messages wrong:

- `REQUIRED_GLIBC="2.35"` — the gate itself
- `"Use a system with glibc 2.35+ for the prebuilt binary"` — recovery guidance; **this actively sends users to the broken 2.36/2.37 case**
- `"Your system has glibc $GLIBC_VERSION but the binary requires glibc 2.35+"` — the post-failure message above

**Expected behavior / suggested fix**

Either would resolve it, and they have different trade-offs:

1. **Bump the declared floor to 2.38** in all three places. Simple, but narrows supported platforms — notably it drops Debian 12, which is still current stable.
2. **Build the release against an older glibc** (e.g. a `manylinux_2_34`/`2_35` image), so the artifact actually honours the advertised 2.35 floor.

Option 2 preserves the existing promise; option 1 just makes it accurate.

**Environment**

- OS: Linux — Debian 11 / 12 / 13 (tested in the official `node:22-*` images)
- Python Version: n/a (the bundled `libpython3.12.so.1.0` in the prebuilt binary)
- APM Version: v0.29.0 and v0.30.0 (latest)
- Installer: `https://aka.ms/apm-unix` as served today
- Arches: `linux-x86_64` and `linux-arm64` (both affected)

issues.title: [BUG] Symlinked .apm/agents silently deploys zero agents
issues.body:
**Describe the bug** When `.apm/agents` is a symlink to another directory inside the same package, `apm install` deploys zero agents. It exits 0 and prints nothing about agents, so the install looks like it succeeded. Skills from the same package deploy normally, which makes the failure hard to spot. The one route that escapes this is a local-path package install, because it dereferences the symlink before the filter runs. `DeployableSourcePlan._is_safe_source_path` calls `has_symlink_component`, which rejects a candidate whose path crosses a symlink at any level (`src/apm_cli/install/deployable_source_plan.py:27`, `src/apm_cli/utils/path_security.py:221`). A symlinked `.apm/agents` directory therefore disqualifies every file under it. `AgentIntegrator.find_agent_files` filters its finds through that plan, gets an empty authorized set, and `integrate_agents_for_target` returns `IntegrationResult(0, 0, 0, [])` with no diagnostic. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["apm install, git dependency"] --> G2["git checkout materializes
.apm/agents as a symlink"] L1["apm install, local path"] --> L2["local_content.py dereferences
the symlink into a real file
PR 1676, v0.19.0"] G2 --> P["DeployableSourcePlan.create"] L2 --> P P --> S["_is_safe_source_path on
.apm/agents/codebase-oracle.agent.md"] S --> H["has_symlink_component
walks every path component"] H -->|"crosses a symlink, true"| DROP["file omitted from plan.paths"] H -->|"no symlink, false"| KEEP["file added to plan.paths"] DROP --> F["find_agent_files,
filter_authorized_files returns empty"] F --> Z["IntegrationResult zero files,
no diagnostic, exit 0"] KEEP --> Y["agents written to .claude/agents"] ``` This inverts a contract that #1668 settled a year ago. That report was the mirror image: a local-path install dropped symlinked skill references while the remote install kept them, and the expected behavior agreed on there was "a symlink whose target resolves inside the package is deployed as a regular file with the target's contents". #1676 (v0.19.0) fixed the local path to match the remote one, and that dereference is still in place at `src/apm_cli/install/phases/local_content.py:277`. #2598 (v0.29.0) then added `DeployableSourcePlan` and `has_symlink_component`, and routed the integrators through it. The remote path has no dereference step, so Git-materialized symlinks now hit the new filter. The two install routes are asymmetric again, in the opposite direction, and the route that #1668 treated as the reference is the broken one. **Reach** Our bundles have shipped `.apm/agents -> ../agents` since May 2026. The authored files live in `agents/` at the package root, next to `skills/`, and `.apm/` holds the typed entry points APM reads. One of our projects locked with 0.14.2 lists 10 `.claude/agents/*.md` paths under `deployed_files`, five per dependency. The same dependencies locked with 0.29.1 list none, and `.claude/agents/` is never created. Skills are not symlink tolerant either, which is worth stating because it shapes the fix. A `.apm/skills -> ../skills` symlink is refused by the same predicate. Skills still deploy because a root-level `skills//SKILL.md` collection is a separately recognized layout (`DeployableSourcePlan.create` reads both `skills/` and `.apm/skills/`), so APM never needs the symlinked path. Agents have only `.apm/agents/` and loose `*.agent.md` at the package root, so they are the primitive that disappears. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph pkg["package as shipped"] A1["agents/*.agent.md"] S1["skills/name/SKILL.md"] AL["symlink .apm/agents to ../agents"] SL["symlink .apm/skills to ../skills"] end AL -->|"only source location
APM reads for agents"| REJ1["rejected, symlink component"] SL -->|"read for skills"| REJ2["rejected, symlink component"] S1 -->|"root skills collection,
a recognized layout"| OK["skills deploy"] A1 -->|"no root-level agents layout exists"| NONE["never read"] REJ1 --> GONE["zero agents deployed"] NONE --> GONE ``` **To Reproduce** Minimal case, no remote needed. A project whose own `.apm/agents` is a real directory deploys its agent: ```bash mkdir -p probe-real/.claude probe-real/.apm/agents && cd probe-real printf 'name: probe-real\nversion: 0.0.0\ndependencies:\n apm: []\n mcp: []\n' > apm.yml printf -- '---\nname: repro-agent\ndescription: A repro agent.\nmodel: sonnet\n---\n\nBody.\n' > .apm/agents/repro-agent.agent.md apm install -v ls .claude/agents/ # repro-agent.md ``` Move the same file to a sibling directory and point `.apm/agents` at it, and nothing deploys: ```bash mkdir -p probe-link/.claude probe-link/agents probe-link/.apm && cd probe-link printf 'name: probe-link\nversion: 0.0.0\ndependencies:\n apm: []\n mcp: []\n' > apm.yml printf -- '---\nname: repro-agent\ndescription: A repro agent.\nmodel: sonnet\n---\n\nBody.\n' > agents/repro-agent.agent.md ln -s ../agents .apm/agents apm install -v ls .claude/agents/ # No such file or directory ``` The same thing happens for a Git dependency, which is how we hit it. Installing a bundle that ships `.apm/agents -> ../agents` produces no `.claude/agents/` and no agent entries in `apm.lock.yaml`. Installing that identical, unmodified checkout with `apm install ` deploys all six of its agents, and `apm_modules/_local//.apm/agents` is a real directory there rather than a symlink. **Expected behavior** The #1668 contract holds on every install route: a symlink resolving inside the package root is deployed as a regular file. `_is_safe_source_path` already calls `ensure_path_within_resolved`, which rejects the case the guard exists for, a link escaping the package. Two options, either would work for us: 1. Dereference in-package symlinks for Git-sourced packages the way `local_content.py` does for local paths, so the two routes agree. 2. Have `has_symlink_component` accept a symlink whose resolved target stays under the package root, and keep rejecting the rest. Failing that, the install has to say something. A package can lose every one of its agents while `apm install` reports success, and no output at any verbosity points at the cause. `AgentIntegrator` already carries a `DiagnosticCollector` and emits `Skipped non-agent Markdown in agents source tree` for files it classifies out, so this path has somewhere to put a message. It took us two sessions to find it by reading the installer source. **Environment** - OS: macOS 26.4.1 (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64) - Python Version: 3.12 (bundled in the release binary) - APM Version: 0.29.1 (1b3d80a). `_is_safe_source_path` is unchanged on `main` at v0.30.0, so this is not fixed there. **Logs** Verbose install of the symlinked case. Nothing about agents at any point, and the plan walk visits no files: ``` [#] Perf: 3 walks, 0 file matches, 0 files visited, 0.001s total walk time [#] Perf: .apm: 3 walk(s) (1ms, 0 files visited, 0 matched) [#] Perf: discovery: 3 call(s) (1 unique base(s), 2 cache hit(s), 66%) ... [*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 0.0s. ``` The real-directory case, same command: ``` Deployed 1 local primitive(s) from .apm/ [#] Perf: 3 walks, 1 file matches, 3 files visited, 0.001s total walk time [#] Perf: .apm: 3 walk(s) (1ms, 3 files visited, 1 matched) ``` **Additional context** We can restructure our bundles so `.apm/agents` is a real directory, and we will if the symlink is meant to be unsupported. Worth saying explicitly either way, because the current behavior reads as a package that installed fine. Related: #1668 and #1676 (the contract and the local-path dereference), #2598 (added `DeployableSourcePlan` and `has_symlink_component`), #2710 (a different Git symlink case, dangling links in sparse-cone subdir installs).

  `_children_by_directory` in-memory indexes built once per compile

- `security/executables.py` -- `resolve_exec_decision` / `_map_grants`

  small number of times per `run_script` invocation (not in a per-item

- `adapters/client/base.py` -- `_should_skip_env_prompts` centralises
  the env/TTY check into one static helper reused by both resolver call
  sites, avoiding drift/duplication rather than causing redundant
  parsing.

No unconditional directory scans, no linear membership tests against a
loop-static list, and no sequential I/O loops without an existing
`ThreadPoolExecutor` were found in the reviewed code paths.

issues.title: [BUG] Claude compilation omits CLAUDE.md from three-level dependencies
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm compile --target claude` does not import dependency `CLAUDE.md` files when the dependency is materialized more than two directory levels below `apm_modules`.

Azure DevOps dependencies use paths such as `apm_modules/<org>/<project>/<repo>`, but Claude compilation only checks `apm_modules/<owner>/<package>/CLAUDE.md`.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install an Azure DevOps dependency that contains a root `CLAUDE.md`.
2. Confirm the dependency is materialized at `apm_modules/org/project/repo/CLAUDE.md`.
3. Run `apm compile --target claude`.
4. Inspect the generated root `CLAUDE.md`.
5. Observe that it does not contain `@apm_modules/org/project/repo/CLAUDE.md`.

A minimal filesystem probe containing both two-level and three-level dependencies returns only:

```text
['@apm_modules/owner/package/CLAUDE.md']
```

**Expected behavior**

The generated root `CLAUDE.md` should include an import for every installed dependency containing a root `CLAUDE.md`, including:

```text
@apm_modules/org/project/repo/CLAUDE.md
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.12.13
 - APM Version: 0.30.0

**Logs**

No error is reported. The dependency import is silently omitted from the generated root `CLAUDE.md`.

**Additional context**

`src/apm_cli/compilation/claude_formatter.py` method `_collect_dependencies` scans exactly two directory levels below `apm_modules` and checks only `<owner>/<package>/CLAUDE.md`.

`src/apm_cli/models/dependency/materialization.py` materializes Azure DevOps dependencies at `<org>/<project>/<repo>` and supports deeper repository paths for other hosts.

Dependency imports should be derived from installed package roots or lockfile/materialization records instead of assuming exactly two path components.

issues.title: [BUG] Codex agent conversion leaves source-relative Markdown links unresolved
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

APM 0.30.0 leaves a source-relative Markdown link unchanged when converting an agent to Codex TOML. The link is valid in the source plugin but points to a nonexistent file relative to the generated agent directory. The same installation correctly rewrites the link in the Copilot output.

The referenced skill is present in the installation; the problem is the link in Codex `developer_instructions`, not missing package content.

## To reproduce

With APM 0.30.0 available, create this `apm.yml` in an otherwise empty directory:

```yaml
name: agent-link-repro
version: 1.0.0
dependencies:
  apm:
    - dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-msbuild#4c72b17fa2c2aaa307d8f1e337ec75cab45ac5c7
```

Run:

```shell
apm install --target copilot,codex
```

The command exits successfully. Generated and installed file paths below are relative to the directory containing `apm.yml`. Relative Markdown link destinations are resolved from the directory containing the respective source or generated agent file.

The [source agent](https://github.com/dotnet/skills/blob/4c72b17fa2c2aaa307d8f1e337ec75cab45ac5c7/plugins/dotnet-msbuild/agents/msbuild-code-review.agent.md) contains this link to an [existing sibling skill](https://github.com/dotnet/skills/blob/4c72b17fa2c2aaa307d8f1e337ec75cab45ac5c7/plugins/dotnet-msbuild/skills/msbuild-antipatterns/SKILL.md):

```markdown
[msbuild-antipatterns skill](../skills/msbuild-antipatterns/SKILL.md)
```

### Actual Codex output

In `.codex/agents/msbuild-code-review.toml`, the parsed `developer_instructions` value retains that exact link. Relative to `.codex/agents/`, its destination is `.codex/skills/msbuild-antipatterns/SKILL.md`, which does not exist.

### Working Copilot comparison

In `.github/agents/msbuild-code-review.agent.md`, APM rewrites the same link to:

```markdown
[msbuild-antipatterns skill](../../apm_modules/dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-msbuild/.apm/skills/msbuild-antipatterns/SKILL.md)
```

That destination exists. The skill is also deployed at `.agents/skills/msbuild-antipatterns/SKILL.md`.

## Expected behavior

A valid in-package Markdown link should remain valid after the agent is converted to Codex TOML and relocated. For this reproduction, resolving the link from the generated agent directory should reach the installed `msbuild-antipatterns/SKILL.md`, as the Copilot output already does.

This report does not require a particular destination layout or a general redesign of agent bundles.

## Environment

- OS: Linux x86-64.
- APM: `0.30.0 (8c2e0d9)`, official standalone release binary.
- Release: [v0.30.0](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/releases/tag/v0.30.0), published September 7, 2026; latest stable release when reproduced on September 12, 2026.

This reproduction inspects generated files only. No Codex or Copilot model session was run, so it does not establish how a model might recover through independent skill discovery.

## Additional context

In the [release's agent integration code](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/8c2e0d9c352e2ed0e8c56b40063a63e1dd4a1937/src/apm_cli/integration/agent_integrator.py#L274-L288), the Codex branch calls `_write_codex_agent` and sets `links_resolved = 0`. Other relevant targets call `copy_agent`, which invokes `resolve_links`. `_write_codex_agent` instead serializes the unchanged Markdown body into `developer_instructions`.

Related reports:

- #1147 is earlier context for preserving in-package relative links. This reproduction isolates the Codex conversion path in the current stable release.
- #2692 concerns broader agent discovery and bundle preservation. Here, the referenced resource is already retained, and the Copilot output links to it correctly.

issues.title: [BUG] apm install fails on Windows: shutil.which(str(directory / name)) never resolves git.exe (PATHEXT not applied)
issues.body:
## What happened

`apm install`/`apm update` fails on Windows with:

```
Failed to download dependency <owner>/<repo>: Failed to clone repository: git executable not found on PATH. Please install git: https://git-scm.com/downloads
```

...even when `git` is installed and resolvable on `PATH` (verified with `git --version` / `(Get-Command git).Source` in the same shell, in both Git Bash and native PowerShell).

## Root cause

`apm_cli/utils/git_env.py`, in `_resolve_trusted_executable()`:

```python
candidate = shutil.which(str(directory / name))
```

On Windows, `shutil.which()` only appends `PATHEXT` extensions (`.EXE`, `.CMD`, …) when the given command has **no directory component**. Once you join a directory onto the name (`str(directory / name)`), `shutil.which` takes the "already a path" branch and checks the literal string for an exact, executable match — it never tries `git.exe`, `git.EXE`, etc. Since the file on disk is `git.exe` and never a bare `git`, the check always fails, for every directory on `PATH`, regardless of whether Git is installed.

Minimal repro (no APM involved):

```python
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

d = Path(r"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd")
shutil.which(str(d / "git"))        # -> None  (this is the current code's call shape)
shutil.which("git", path=str(d))    # -> 'C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.EXE'  (correct)
```

Same failure mode affects `get_gh_executable()` (`gh` resolution) for the same reason.

## Fix

Pass the command name and directory separately so `shutil.which`'s Windows `PATHEXT` handling actually runs:

```python
# apm_cli/utils/git_env.py, _resolve_trusted_executable()
- candidate = shutil.which(str(directory / name))
+ candidate = shutil.which(name, path=str(directory))
```

Verified this one-line change resolves `git`/`gh` correctly via the existing per-directory loop, with the existing trusted-directory exclusion logic (`_executable_exclusion_root`) untouched.

## Environment

- `apm-cli` 0.30.0 (`pip install apm-cli`)
- Windows 11, git 2.43.0.windows.1 (`C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe`), gh CLI installed
- Reproduced identically in Git Bash and native `powershell.exe`

issues.title: Add per-server targets: field to MCP dependency objects (like ApmDependency.targets)
issues.body:
## Problem

`dependencies.mcp` entries (`McpDependency`, manifest schema §4.2.2) have no
`targets:`/`target:` field, unlike `dependencies.apm` entries
(`ApmDependency`), which do support `targets: list<string>` to scope a
package dependency to a subset of the project's active install targets
(schema §4.1.2).

This makes it impossible to declare, inside `apm.yml`, an MCP server that
should deploy to only some of a project's configured harnesses. Concretely:
our `apm.yml` has `targets: [claude, cursor]` (needed because we also manage
skills that reach both harnesses). We have two MCP servers
(`http`, no secrets) that are genuinely Cursor-only — they point at
local-dev-only endpoints Claude Code has no equivalent workflow for. There is
no way to declare them under `dependencies.mcp:` without a bare `apm install`
silently deploying them into Claude's `.mcp.json` too, since the project's
top-level `targets:` is the only scope that currently applies to an MCP
dependency.

We confirmed there is no workaround:
- Passing `--target cursor` at `apm mcp install <name> ...` only scopes the
  *initial write*; the field it persists to `apm.yml` has no per-entry
  targets, so the very next bare `apm install` (using the project's top-level
  `targets:`) deploys it to every configured target again.
- A hand-added `targets:` key on an `McpDependency` object is silently
  dropped as an unrecognized passthrough field per §4.2.2's own documented
  guardrail ("passthrough key... never overwrite a value the target adapter
  set itself" / reserved-key rejection), not honored.

## Request

Add an optional `targets: list<string>` field to the `McpDependency` object
form, mirroring `ApmDependency.targets` (§4.1.2): "Restricts which install
targets receive this dependency's target-scoped primitives. Omitted = all
active install targets. Effective reach = install targets INTERSECT this
list."

## Context / repro

Manifest schema doc confirms the asymmetry:
https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/manifest-schema/#412-object-form
(ApmDependency has `targets`) vs
https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/manifest-schema/#422-object-form
(McpDependency does not).

Reproduced against `apm` 0.30.0: declaring two `http` MCP servers under
`dependencies.mcp:` with a project `targets: [claude, cursor]`, then running
a bare `apm install`, deploys both into `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`
identically — there is no way to keep one Cursor-only.

## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-18
**APM Version**: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.31.0 (c6d99eb)
**Commands Inspected**: 27 (`apm --help`, `init`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`, `deps`, `deps list`, `deps tree`, `deps info`, `deps clean`, `deps update`, `deps why`, `mcp`, `mcp list`, `mcp search`, `mcp show`, `mcp install`, `config`, `config set`, `config get`, `config list`, `runtime`, `runtime setup`, plus invalid-argument checks for `install`, `deps info`, `config set`, `mcp show`, `runtime setup`)

### Medium Severity

#### `apm mcp install` doc omits `--trust-transitive-mcp` from the forwarded-options table

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`

      --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]

      --mcp-version VER      Pin registry entry to a specific version

      --trust-transitive-mcp Trust MCP servers from transitive dependencies
      --dev / --dry-run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy

  - Doc excerpt (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/mcp.md`, "Forwarded install options" table):

    | `--mcp-version VER` | Pin the registry entry to a specific version. |

    | `--dry-run` | Resolve and print without writing `apm.yml`. |
    | `--force` | Overwrite an existing entry. |
    | `-g`, `--global` | Install through `~/.apm/apm.yml` into global-capable runtimes. |
    | `--no-policy` | Skip policy checks. |
    | `--verbose`, `-v` | Verbose output. |
    ```
    (No `--trust-transitive-mcp` row; also missing `-t, --target`, though that one is implied elsewhere in the doc's synopsis/examples.)
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a `--trust-transitive-mcp` row to the "Forwarded install options" table in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/mcp.md`, e.g. `| \`--trust-transitive-mcp\` | Trust self-defined MCP servers from transitive dependencies (skip re-declaration requirement). |`, matching the description used in `apm install --help`.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Installation & version check**: `apm --version` and `apm --help` work correctly; top-level command list is accurate.
- **Core commands** (`init`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`): help text is well-structured, uses consistent `Usage:` / `Options:` layout, and flag descriptions read naturally.
- **`deps` subcommands** (`list`, `tree`, `info`, `clean`, `update`, `why`): all flags cross-checked against `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md` with no discrepancies (aside from the `mcp install` finding above, which is unrelated to `deps`).

- **`runtime` subcommands** (`setup`): matches `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/runtime.md`, including the `{copilot|codex|gemini|llm}` choice validation.

- **Exit behavior**: Invalid invocations (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no argument, `apm config set` with no arguments, `apm mcp show` with no argument, `apm runtime setup badruntime`) all produce clean `Usage:` + `Error:` messages and exit code `2` -- no stack traces or unhandled exceptions observed.
- **Typos/grammar**: No spelling errors, doubled words, or placeholder/TODO text found in any inspected help output.
- **README.md cross-reference**: Commands and flags referenced in `README.md` (`apm install`, `apm compile -t copilot`, `apm install --mcp ... --transport http`, `apm marketplace add`, `apm lock export --format cyclonedx|spdx`) all exist and behave as described.

issues.title: [BUG] global audit scans unmanaged Codex session history for hidden Unicode
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

APM 0.31.0's global audit scans Codex session history under `~/.codex/sessions/` as deployed content. A literal `U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE` in an unmanaged session file causes `apm audit --ci` to fail its content-integrity check and recommend `apm audit --strip`.

This reproduces with an empty global dependency list. APM did not install or record ownership of the session file.

**To Reproduce**

1. In an isolated test home, create `~/.apm/apm.yml`:

   ```yaml
   name: global-profile
   version: 1.0.0
   targets: [codex]
   dependencies:
     apm: []
     mcp: []
   ```

2. Create `~/.codex/sessions/unmanaged.jsonl` with a JSON string containing a literal U+202E character. For example, this Python expression produces the file contents (the character must be literal, not a JSON escape):

   ```python
   json.dumps({"message": "safe" + chr(0x202E) + "reversed"}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
   ```

3. Run `apm lock -g`, then run `apm audit --ci --no-policy --no-drift` from `~/.apm` in that same test home.

4. Observe exit code 1 and the content-integrity finding below.

**Expected behavior**

Audit excludes unrelated Codex application state such as session history. Hidden-Unicode scanning should still cover deployable primitive locations, including unrecorded files in those locations, and explicit deployment claims.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: macOS
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- APM Version: 0.31.0 (Homebrew); also reproduced with current `main`

**Logs**

```text
content-integrity: 1 file(s) with critical hidden Unicode
-- run 'apm audit --strip' to clean Unicode

content-integrity details:
  - unicode: .codex/sessions/unmanaged.jsonl

[x] 1 of 8 check(s) failed
```

**Additional context**

The [Codex target](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/98616b9430140275a3a7c8fefb25d8d111cecc4e/src/apm_cli/integration/targets.py#L781-L801) declares `.codex` as its root. [`install_governance`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/98616b9430140275a3a7c8fefb25d8d111cecc4e/src/apm_cli/install/manifest_reconcile.py#L147-L175) includes the whole root prefix, and the [audit scanner](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/98616b9430140275a3a7c8fefb25d8d111cecc4e/src/apm_cli/security/file_scanner.py#L146-L179) recursively scans that prefix. This brings session history into the scan despite it being outside the target's primitive locations.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report - 2026-09-21
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-21
**APM Version**: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.31.0 (98616b9)
**Commands Inspected**: 22 (`--help` for: `apm`, `init`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`, `deps`, `deps list`, `deps tree`, `deps info`, `deps clean`, `deps update`, `mcp`, `mcp search`, `mcp show`, `mcp install`, `config`, `config set`, `config get`, `config list`, `runtime`, `runtime setup`), plus cross-referenced `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/*.md` and `README.md`, and live-tested `apm init`, `apm config`, `apm view`, `apm list`, and error paths (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no argument, `apm config set` with no arguments).

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 1 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm init` footer prints a broken/truncated "Star:" link
- **Command**: `apm init` (also `apm init --yes`, any successful init)
- **Problem**: The success footer prints `Docs: <url>  |  Star: ` with nothing after `Star:` on that line -- the actual GitHub URL (`https://github.com/microsoft/apm`) gets pushed to its own line below, because the combined string is longer than the detected terminal width and Rich soft-wraps mid-label. In a real terminal (80 cols) and when output is redirected to a file, the result is a dangling `Star:` label followed by a blank-looking gap and the URL orphaned on the next line, which reads as broken/incomplete output.
- **Evidence** (from `apm init --yes` in an 80-column terminal and when redirected to a file):
  ```
    Docs: (microsoft.github.io/redacted)  |  Star: 
  https://github.com/microsoft/apm
  ```
  Source (`src/apm_cli/commands/init.py:427-437`):
  ```python
  console.print(
      "  Docs: (microsoft.github.io/redacted)  |  "
      "Star: https://github.com/microsoft/apm",
      style="dim",
  )
  ```
  The string is a single un-wrapped concatenation with no `no_wrap`/`overflow` handling, so Rich's default word-wrap breaks it awkwardly once the line exceeds console width.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either shorten the line (e.g. `Docs: <url> | GitHub: <url>` on one line only if it reliably fits 80 cols), split "Docs" and "Star" onto two separate `console.print` calls, or pass `overflow="ignore"` / disable wrapping (`soft_wrap=True` is not enough; consider `Text(..., no_wrap=True)` or shortening the copy) so the label and its URL never separate.

---

### Medium Severity

#### Inconsistent trailing punctuation in subcommand-group summary lines
- **Command**: `apm mcp --help`, `apm --help`, `apm deps --help`
- **Problem**: Command-group listings mix terminated and unterminated one-line summaries inconsistently. In `apm mcp --help`, the `install` subcommand summary ends with a period while `list`, `search`, and `show` do not. The same inconsistency appears at the top level of `apm --help` (e.g. `config` and `pack` end with a period; `deps`, `cache`, `compile` do not) and in other groups.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp --help
  Commands:
    install  Add an MCP server to apm.yml.
    list     List all available MCP servers
    search   Search MCP servers in registry
    show     Show detailed MCP server information
  ```
  ```
  $ apm --help
  Commands:
    ...
    config        Configure APM CLI.
    deps          Manage APM package dependencies
    ...
    pack          Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.
    plugin        Scaffold and manage plugins (plugin-author workflows)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize all Click `help=` summary strings (the short one-liners shown in group listings) to either always omit the trailing period or always include it. Given the majority currently omit it, dropping the period from `config`, `pack`, `publish`, `self-update`, `targets`, `lifecycle`, `unpack`, and `mcp install` would restore consistency.

---

### Low Severity

#### `-y, --yes` flag present on only 3 of ~15 commands that perform destructive or state-changing actions, with no documented rationale for the split
- **Command**: `apm init`, `apm update`, `apm deps clean` (have `-y/--yes`) vs. `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm compile --clean`, `apm deps update`, `apm mcp install`, `apm config set/unset` (no `-y/--yes`, and no confirmation prompt observed either)
- **Problem**: Some destructive/state-mutating commands expose `-y, --yes` to skip prompts, while others with equally consequential effects (e.g. `apm uninstall`, which deletes deployed primitives across every harness) have no `--yes`/confirmation flag at all -- because they apparently never prompt interactively in the first place. This isn't necessarily a bug, but the flag's presence is inconsistent across commands with similar risk profiles, and it isn't called out anywhere in the docs why some commands need `-y` and others don't.
- **Evidence**: `apm uninstall --help` output has no `-y/--yes`:
  ```
  Options:
    --dry-run      Preview removal plan (pre-uninstall scripts still run)
    -v, --verbose  Show detailed removal information
    -g, --global   Remove from user scope (~/.apm/) instead of the current
                   project
    --help         Show this message and exit.
  ```
  vs. `apm deps clean --help`, a comparably destructive command, which does have it:
  ```
  Options:
    --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
    -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt
    --help     Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either add `-y/--yes` to `apm uninstall` for parity (if it should support non-interactive skip-confirmation in some contexts), or add a short note in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/uninstall.md` clarifying that `apm uninstall` never prompts and therefore has no `--yes` flag, to preempt confusion when compared against sibling destructive commands.

#### Inconsistent verbose/dry-run wording across near-duplicate commands
- **Command**: various (`install`, `update`, `deps update`, `compile`, `run`)
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` flag description text differs across commands doing conceptually similar things, e.g.:
  - `install`: "Show detailed installation information"
  - `update`: "Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics"
  - `deps update`: "Show detailed update information"
  - `compile`: "Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis"
  - `run`, `mcp search`, `mcp show`, `runtime setup` (n/a), `deps list`/`tree` (no `-v` at all): plain "Show detailed output"
  This is expected to some extent (different commands show different detail), but the wording style is inconsistent (some are one-size "Show detailed output", others are hand-tailored), which is a minor polish item rather than a functional bug.
- **Evidence**: see `grep -h "\-v, --verbose" *.txt` output collected during this audit (available on request); no single canonical phrasing pattern is followed.
- **Suggested Fix**: Low priority. If touched during other doc/CLI work, consider a light style pass so `--verbose` descriptions follow a shared pattern like "Show detailed (topic) information" everywhere it doesn't already.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Installation and version reporting**: `apm --version` and `apm --help` work correctly; the CLI installed cleanly via `uv sync` (Python 3.12).
- **Error handling**: All tested invalid invocations (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no package, `apm config set` with no arguments) produced clean Click usage errors and exit code 2 -- no stack traces or crashes.
- **Documentation cross-reference**: Every command exercised in this audit (`init`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`, `deps` + subcommands, `mcp` + subcommands, `config` + subcommands, `runtime` + subcommands) has a corresponding, accurate page under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`, with flags, defaults, and examples matching the live `--help` output. The `README.md` link to `reference/cli-commands` resolves via a documented redirect in `docs/astro.config.mjs` (`/reference/cli-commands` -> `/reference/cli/install`), so it is not a broken link.
- **`-g, --global`, `--dry-run` semantics**: Consistent behavior and clearly worded descriptions across all commands that support them.
- **`apm config`**: Behaves exactly as documented; `apm config` (no subcommand) prints the merged table, `apm config list` is a proper alias for `apm config get` with no key.
- **`apm runtime`**: All four subcommands (`setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove`) match their documentation precisely, including the experimental-flag caveat.

> [!WARNING]

> <summary>Firewall blocked 2 domains</summary>
>

>
> - `astral.sh`
> - `index.crates.io`

> network:

>     - "astral.sh"
>     - "index.crates.io"
> ```

> See [Network Configuration](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/network/) for more information.

issues.title: [BUG] Codex hooks miss the required nested hooks level
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When APM installs a portable `SessionStart` hook for the Codex target, it writes the command handler directly into the event array instead of converting it to Codex's native nested hook structure.

APM currently generates:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "type": "command",
        "command": "echo session-start"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Codex expects an intermediate matcher-group object containing a `hooks` array:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "echo session-start"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The generated configuration therefore does not conform to Codex's hook schema.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a project configured for Codex:

   ```yaml
   name: codex-hook-reproduction
   version: 0.0.0
   targets:
     - codex
   ```

2. Add `.apm/hooks/check.json` containing:

   ```json
   {
     "hooks": {
       "SessionStart": [
         {
           "type": "command",
           "command": "echo session-start"
         }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```

3. Run:

   ```bash
   apm install --target codex
   ```

4. Inspect `.codex/hooks.json`.

5. Observe that the command handler is written directly under `SessionStart[]` instead of under the required nested `hooks[]` array.

**Expected behavior**

APM should translate portable hooks to Codex's native three-level structure:

```text
event -> matcher group -> hooks[] -> handler
```

For `SessionStart`, the matcher may be omitted, but the intermediate group and its nested `hooks` array are still required.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Python version: 3.14.7
- APM version: 0.31.0
- VSCode version: N/A

**Logs**

APM reports that the hook was integrated successfully:

```text
1 hook(s) integrated -> .codex/hooks.json
```

No installation error is reported, despite the incompatible output shape.

Complete logs:

```text
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
Parsed apm.yml: 0 APM deps, 0 MCP deps
Resolved 0 direct dependencies (no transitive)
Phase: resolve -> 0.003s
[i] Could not determine org from git remote; policy auto-discovery skipped
Phase: policy_gate -> 0.020s
[i] Targets: codex  (source: --target flag)
Phase: targets -> 0.002s
Copilot native registration: unavailable (copilot target not selected)
Phase: copilot_activate -> 0.000s
Phase: policy_target_check -> 0.000s
Phase: download -> 0.000s
  [+] <project root> (local)
Integrating local .apm/ content...
  |-- 1 hook(s) integrated -> .codex/hooks.json
  |   SessionStart: runs echo session-start (check.json)
  |   Hook JSON (check.json -> hooks.json):
  |     {
  |       "hooks": {
  |         "SessionStart": [
  |           {
  |             "command": "echo session-start",
  |             "type": "command"
  |           }
  |         ]
  |       }
  |     }
Deployed 1 local primitive(s) from .apm/
Phase: integrate -> 0.005s
Phase: cleanup -> 0.000s
Phase: post_deps_local -> 0.000s
Phase: audit -> 0.000s
Phase: copilot_plugins -> 0.000s
[#] Perf: 3 walks, 0 file matches, 3 files visited, 0.001s total walk time
[#] Perf:   .apm: 3 walk(s) (1ms, 3 files visited, 0 matched)
[#] Perf: discovery: 2 call(s) (1 unique base(s), 1 cache hit(s), 50%)
Integrated 1 hook(s)
Phase: finalize -> 0.000s
No MCP dependencies found in apm.yml
No LSP dependencies found in apm.yml
  [i] Skipped inactive experimental resolver for target 'copilot-cowork' during lockfile reconciliation.
    +- To include it, enable 'copilot-cowork' and select target 'copilot-cowork' for this install.
  [i] Skipped inactive experimental resolver for target 'copilot-app' during lockfile reconciliation.
    +- To include it, enable 'copilot-app' and select target 'copilot-app' for this install.
[*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 0.1s.
```

**Additional context**

The Codex documentation describes hooks as three levels: event, matcher group, and handler. It also defines `hooks.<Event>[].hooks` as the array of hook handlers:

- [Codex hooks: configuration shape](https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks#config-shape)
- [Codex configuration reference](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference)
- [Codex advanced configuration: hooks](https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-advanced#hooks)

The integration pipeline already applies target-specific native renderers for Claude, Gemini, and Antigravity. Codex currently has no equivalent renderer, so portable flat entries pass through unchanged.

issues.title: [perf-scan] 2026-09-25 -- performance opportunities found
issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-09-25

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
1 finding identified.

### Findings

#### [F] Sequential independent I/O -- src/apm_cli/commands/install.py:295-484

- Current: O(n) sequential network round-trips -- `_resolve_package_references`
  iterates `packages` one at a time (line 295) and, for each package that
  isn't registry-routed or git-semver-eligible, calls
  `_validate_package_exists` (line 466) synchronously. That function
  performs a blocking GitHub/ADO REST API probe (`requests.get`, see
  `install/validation.py:693` and `:796`) or a shallow git fetch
  (`github_downloader_validation.py:770-806`) per package, with no data
  dependency between iterations (each package's accessibility check is
  independent of the others).
- Proposed: O(1) wall-clock round-trips (bounded by `max_workers`) using a
  `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor`, the same pattern already applied
  in `commands/outdated.py:713-761` (`_check_parallel`/`_check_parallel_plain`)
  and `deps/apm_resolver.py:830` for analogous per-dependency network probes.
- Fix: Wrap the per-package accessibility probe (and its git-semver /
  registry-ref branches, which are cheap/local) in a bounded
  `ThreadPoolExecutor.map`/`as_completed` call inside
  `_resolve_package_references`, preserving per-package error handling
  (`GitUrlRewriteError`/`GitUrlRewriteProbeError`) and outcome ordering, so
  `apm install pkg1 pkg2 pkg3 ...` validates all packages concurrently
  instead of one network round-trip at a time.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (485 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)
